News.title: Mass ‘murderer’ who ‘killed 4 members of ex’s family before claiming he’s in the FBI’ is sentenced over jail fight
News.content:
A MAN accused of massacring four members of his girlfriend’s family has been convicted over a separate prison attack in which an inmate said he was stabbed 17 times.

Austin Drummond, 29, escaped an attempted first-degree murder conviction but was found guilty of the lesser charge of attempted voluntary manslaughter and possessing contraband inside a prison.



The verdict came after a two-day trial in Carroll County, Tennessee, over an August 2023 fight at the Northwest Correctional Complex.

Drummond had been behind bars when prosecutors say he and fellow inmate Andre Brown attacked Timothy Singleton.



Singleton told jurors he had been talking on the phone when he was blindsided and repeatedly stabbed.

He said he suffered 17 wounds, including injuries to his head, back and chest.



A nurse who treated Singleton documented wounds to his hand, arm, shoulder and scalp as well as multiple injuries to his back.

Drummond denied trying to kill him when he took the stand in his own defense.

He said he had heard Singleton was planning to attack him following threats involving money and claimed he acted to protect himself.

Drummond also told jurors that he never intended to kill Singleton.



Jurors deliberated for about two hours before clearing Drummond of the original attempted first-degree murder count.

Brown was also acquitted of attempted first-degree murder but convicted of facilitation of attempted voluntary manslaughter.

He was found not guilty of possessing contraband in the prison.

Drummond and Brown are scheduled to be sentenced in Lake County on August 31.



The case is separate from the four murder charges that have made Drummond one of Tennessee’s most notorious defendants.

He is accused of killing Cortney Rose, 38, Rose’s daughter Adrianna Williams, 20, her 15-year-old son Braydon Williams, and Adrianna’s boyfriend James “Matthew” Wilson, 21, in July 2025.

All four were found shot dead in Lake County.

Drummond knew the victims through his relationship with Rose’s sister, Kaitlyn Speed, who was pregnant with his child at the time of the killings.



Hours before the bodies were discovered, Adrianna and Wilson’s seven-month-old baby was found alive in a car seat outside a stranger’s home around 40 miles away.

Drummond was captured in Jackson after a weeklong manhunt and has pleaded not guilty to the murder and kidnapping charges.

Prosecutors have said they intend to seek the death penalty.

The accused killer has since made extraordinary claims about what he was doing before the four deaths.

In court filings this year, Drummond alleged that he had been working as a confidential informant for state and federal law enforcement.



He claimed his cooperation began after an April 2025 meeting involving an assistant district attorney, FBI and ATF agents and a Tennessee prison narcotics investigator.

Drummond submitted what he said were letters and emails supporting his account, although WBBJ said it had not independently verified the documents.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He also claimed the four people he is accused of killing were connected to the investigation and that his identity as an informant had been exposed before their deaths.

Drummond remains in custody while the quadruple murder case moves toward trial.

News.title: Moment yob smashes cop’s windscreen after hurling glass bottles at car… before admitting ‘I don’t know why I did that’
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a yob smashes a cop’s windscreen after hurling glass bottles.

An officer was responding to a call out in Aberdare in South Wales when pedestrian Mark Fraser, 40, targeted the vehicle.



Heart-stopping footage shows the bottles, in a blue carrier bag, hurtling toward the car.

The officer had been responding to an emergency call when, out of nowhere, the bottles smash into the windscreen.



The windscreen completely splinters, blinding the officer and forcing him to pull over.

Fraser was immediately put in cuffs on the roadside as he told the cop: “I don’t know why I did that.”

The officer responds, telling Fraser: “I don’t know why you’ve done it either.

“I’m driving down here, responding to a G1, and now I can’t because I’m dealing with you – you could have killed me, mate.”



Furious, he leads Fraser to the front of the motor to show the damage caused.

The entire windscreen is shattered before Fraser is placed under arrest.

South Wales Police said the incident caused around £900 of damage to the vehicle, and put the officer in harm’s way.

In a court appearance on August 5, Fraser admitted to criminal damage by recklessly endangering life

The 40-year-old was sentenced to three years in prison, suspended for three years.



He was also ordered to complete 250 hours of unpaid work and to pay over £6000 in compensation.

South Wales Police posted video of the incident on social media, adding: “The damage cost hundreds of pounds to fix.

“It also shows that even as our officers put themselves in harm’s way every day, sometimes danger can come from unexpected places.”

News.title: Two brothers who ploughed head-on into boy, 9, and his dad, 41, after losing control while racing at 100mph are jailed
News.content:
RACING KILLERS Two brothers who ploughed head-on into boy, 9, and his dad, 41, after losing control while racing at 100mph are jailed

TWO brothers who ploughed head-on into a boy and his dad after losing control while racing at 100mph have been jailed.

Dad-of-two Rhys Jenkins, 41, was killed in the crash and his son Ioan, 9, was airlifted to hospital from the wreckage of the crash scene.



The doting father and son were travelling to see their first Wales rugby game together against Australia – but never made it to the stadium.

The two brothers – both working as opticians – were racing their powerful BMW X3 and sporty Audi S4 when the father and son were hit head-on.



A court heard their high-speed driving was a “car crash waiting to happen” as they sped “aggressively” along a country road at estimated speeds of up to 100mph.

Abubakr Ben Yusaf, 29, and Umar Ben Yusaf, 34, denied all charges during an eight day trial at Mold Crown Court but were found guilty.

Abubakr was jailed for 14 years and his brother Umar jailed for 2 years 9 months.

Prosecutor David Mainstone said the crash happened when one of the cars lost control and Mr Jenkins “couldn’t avoid the collision.”



He said the father and son “paid a terrible price” for the fact the brothers had been driving “with no consideration for other road users”.

Police arrived at the scene but both men from Manchester had fled on the Powys road in the Welsh country.

The jury at Mold Crown Court was told that the brothers were in separate cars on the A483 when the crash happened.

The BMW driven by Abubakr Ben Yusaf was in the collision with Mr Jenkins’ vehicle.

He was found guilty of causing death by dangerous driving, while his brother Umar Ben Yusaf, was found guilty of the lesser charge of causing death and serious injury by careless driving.



The younger brother was also found guilty of causing death while driving uninsured while Umar was found not guilty of causing death and serious injury by dangeous driving.

Abubakr was remanded in custody until sentencing on July 27 and his older brother given bail.

Mr Mainstone said Mr Jenkins was driving his wife’s Toyota Yaris entirely properly in the other direction with son Ioan in the passenger seat when the car was hit head on by the BMW and Mr Jenkins died at the scene.



Ioan was airlifted to Alder Hey Children’s Hospital in Liverpool with serious injuries in November last year at Belan between Welshpool and Newtown.

The court heard that the brothers would often do locum work in Wales and were driving 80 miles away from the home they share.

Mr Jenkins, from Deuddw, Powys, was described by loved ones as a “devoted family man” to his wife Carrie, sons Ioan and Gruff, and a “much-loved” son, brother and uncle.

The family of the highly respected sportsman, who refereed rugby games around Wales and in New Zealand, said his death was “absolutely devastating for us all.”

Rugby referee Mr Jenkins had become a “hugely valued and much loved” member and junior coach at Caereinion Old Boys Rugby Association (COBRA), based in Meifod.



Speaking after the verdict, widow Carrie Jenkins, said: “Following the conviction, I would like to thank the court, the jury, the CPS, police and all those involved in this trial, including the many witnesses who came forward.

“The loss of Rhys in such an unexpected and unnecessary way has been devastating, but our focus as a family has been to rebuild our lives, and to make the most of each day, as Rhys would have wanted, with the support of our friends and community.

“I hope the publicity surrounding the Crown Court case highlights to others the dangers of driving at speed, and acts as a reminder that we all have a responsibility when we get behind a wheel.”

Sergeant Sara John from the Serious Collision Investigation Unit said: “The sentences passed today cannot undo the tragic loss suffered by Rhys’s family, who have shown remarkable strength throughout this investigation and court process.

“I hope that today’s outcome provides them with some closure as they begin to move forward with their lives, which have been changed forever.”



She added that the actions of Abubakr and Umar Yusaf were “catastrophic” and “the impact of their actions can never be underestimated”.

Joanne Brine, solicitor for Carrie Jenkins said: “This has been an unimaginably distressing time for Mrs Jenkins, coping with a life-changing situation which she has handled with courage and grace as she, her children and their wider family have come to terms with the devasting loss of a much-loved husband and father,

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Nothing will ever heal the overwhelming pain of his loss, but they continue to navigate their future in the best way possible, with the invaluable support of their wider community.

“We will continue to support the family as they pursue civil redress for the actions which lead to Rhys’ untimely death.”

News.title: Huge blaze that ripped through fashion outlet in city centre probed as arson after inferno started in caravan next door
News.content:
A HUGE fire that ripped through a city centre fashion outlet is being probed by cops as arson after the inferno started in a caravan next door.

Emergency services descended on a commercial premises in Salford, Greater Manchester, on Wednesday evening.



Shocking images showed a Marc Darcy suit shop on Bury New Road completely engulfed as fire crews battled the blaze.

Flames could be seen pouring from the windows of the building with huge plumes of black smoke billowing into the air.



Cops were called to the scene at 1.50am on Thursday after an alarm was activated at the premises.

They revealed they arrived to fire crews battling a fire at a caravan next to the property which quickly spread.



Greater Manchester Police (GMP) are now treating the incident as arson and are urging any witnesses to come forward.

The blaze is being treated as a “targeted incident” but cops do not believe there is a wider risk to the public.

They added that “extensive damage” was inflicted on the caravan, the building and some cars parked nearby.

Detective Inspector Paul Davies from Salford CID said: “This was a huge fire that caused extensive damage to a commercial property and several vehicles. Thankfully, no one was injured in this incident.

“We’re treating this as arson and we’re appealing for anyone who was in the area at the time, or who may have witnessed anything suspicious, to come forward.



“We’re particularly keen to hear from anyone with CCTV, dashcam, doorbell or mobile phone footage from the evening of Wednesday 5 August or Thursday 6 August that could assist our investigation.”

Video footage shows the shocking moment a section of the burning building comes crashing down.

Fire crews rushed to respond and battled the fire for several hours before bringing it under control.

A stretch of Bury New Road was closed as firefighters remained at the scene throughout the night.

Residents living in the area were urged to stay away and keep their windows and doors closed as plumes of smoke poured from the blaze.



A statement on the Marc Darcy website read: “Important notice. Due to a fire at our premises, we are temporarily unable to accept any new order.

“We sincerely apologise for the inconvenience and will reopen ordering as soon as possible. Thank you for your understanding.”

Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said at the time: “Firefighters are currently tackling a large fire at a commercial building on Hilton Street in Salford.



“Due to the large amount of smoke in the area, residents are advised to keep doors and windows closed and avoid the area.

“Bury New Road remains closed while crews work to extinguish the fire.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Anyone with information is asked to contact Greater Manchester Police on 0161 856 5224, via 101, or through their Live Chat service, quoting incident number 223 of August 6.

Information can also be reported anonymously to the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Two having a drink at bar crushed by man who jumped from apartment on Spanish hols island as they’re rushed to hospital
News.content:
PLUNGE HORROR Two having a drink at bar crushed by man who jumped from apartment on Spanish hols island as they’re rushed to hospital

TWO men drinking at a Majorcan bar have been crushed after a man jumped from a 12th-floor apartment and landed on them.

The pair were injured in Palma, Majorca, when they were suddenly struck by the falling person.

4 Credit: Google



It is understood the incident occurred just before 4pm on Friday by a high-rise building in a residential area near Barcelona Square.

Emergency crews desperately tried to revive the jumper for almost an hour with photos seen by The Sun showing medics crouched over the injured.



The man smashed into a tree near the ground – slightly cushioning his fall – before smacking onto the table.

The two men, 29 and 32, are reported to be Colombian workers who were having drinks at the location after their shift had finished.

The bar table was completely crushed, sending everything on the table flying as the falling man impacted the pair.

The 29-year-old patron suffered serious injuries, while the 22-year-old sustained minor injuries.



A witness said: “He fell onto the table but he seems to have hit one of them almost full-on, who ended up laid out on the floor and appeared to be in very serious condition.”

Local reports said the man had been arguing with his partner shortly before he jumped.

Witnesses say they saw him taking a “running start” before leaping over the edge.

The alarm was raised just moments before the fall when police were called as the concierge grew concerned about the arguing couple.

Shortly after it is understood he decided to jump from the rooftop.



One resident said: “I don’t understand how he got up there; it’s locked and we don’t have regular access.”

Emergency services rushed to the scene and paramedics performed life-saving CPR on the man who fell from the 12th floor before taking him to hospital.

He and the 29-year-old worker were transported to Son Espases Hospital.

It is believed the falling man is around 40-years-old.

The nationalities of the three men has not yet been officially confirmed by the cops.



Occurring in a busy residential area, the shocking incident has stirred the local community.

One person said the scene was “awful”.

Another local said: “The table was broken and the chairs crushed, I saw how they were resuscitating the man who landed on the other two.

“He was on the floor and four paramedics were trying to revive him.

“It was very intense.”



A police investigation was has been launched with officers cordoning off the area to gather information.

Forensic investigators are currently inspecting the building.

In July 2020 a Spanish gym owner was killed when a British holidaymaker landed on top of him after a seventh-floor Costa del Sol hotel plunge.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Antonio Gonzalez, 43, died instantly in the horror incident.

His hotel worker wife Sonia was sitting beside him when Tony Holmes, 49, landed on top of him as they enjoyed an after-dinner drink with friends on the Melia Don Pepe terrace in Marbella.

News.title: Bosses could get incentives to hire young workers in huge shake-up plans to cut number of idle teens
News.content:
JOBS tsar Alan Milburn is drawing up plans for business to employ young people to tackle the youth inactivity crisis.

The Labour grandee is working on an incentives for bosses such as major construction sites to help reduce the numbers not earning or learning.



Mr Milburn delivered an interim report on the matter in May which included how infrastructure projects bring in a large proportion of their workforce from overseas.

PM Andy Burnham has already declared he is “on a mission” to cut the number as he plans to open up new technical education for kids as young as 14.



But a source close to the review said: “The interim report is clear that government needs to help influence employer behaviour and the systems that support young people into work, not just leave it to chance.

“The review is looking at what more can be done to minimise risks and maximise incentives for employers to get more young people into work.”



The focus comes as unemployed youngsters are living within walking distance of big infrastructure projects – but are still finding it impossible to get their career up and running.

Taxpayer-funded projects alone in the East of England – including the Sizewell C nuclear power plant – are worth £220 billion over the next ten years.

However, the region has one in ten 16-24 year-olds NEETs – not in education, employment or training, figures show.

There are currently one in eight young people classed as Neets but this figure is predicted to be one in six by 2031.



Just two in every hundred 16-24 year-olds on Universal Credit are employed in construction despite huge strides made by government funded schemes to increase the number.

Julia Pyke, Chair of Agilia Infrastructure Partners and ex-Managing Director of Sizewell C last night said: “We’re spending billions on infrastructure while more than a million young people are out of work.

She added: “Why aren’t we better at joining the dots?

“Lots of project teams including Sizewell are working hard to improve things.

“Yet the sheer number of young people out of work and skills shortages in the construction industry tell us that projects are passing over young people on their doorsteps.

“The jobs are there. The investment is there. What’s missing is a decision to give enough priority, early in the planning for projects, to give more local people a genuine route in.”



Labour faces serious accusations that they haven’t helped the issue by hiking the minimum wage which has been seen as a big driver of young people left without work.

Mr Milburn has also said that primary schools in England should be made to identify children at risk of leaving school at 16 without landing a job.

He said that Ministers need to “make someone responsible” for looking out for kids who risked becoming a ‘NEET’.

News.title: UK weather: Temperatures to soar again to 36C highs as Met Office confirms another ‘widespread heatwave’
News.content:
TEMPERATURES are set to hit highs of 36C next week as another record breaking heatwave arrives for swathes of the country.

The mercury will begin rising over the weekend before peaking on Thursday next week in East Anglia and the southeast.



Temperatures could reach 27C on Friday and as high as 30C on Saturday, before climbing into the low 30s in southern and south-east England on Sunday.

Forecasters said the weekend will see a north-south split in the weather with Scotland and Northern Ireland likely to see spells of heavy rain, while England and Wales will remain largely dry, sunny and increasingly warm.



Heat health alerts will be in place as experts warn that the hot weather is likely to affect the wellbeing of the population.

This summer has seen two record-breaking heatwaves, in May and June, and two more heatwaves in July which have fuelled drought and wildfires.



The highest temperature of the year was 38C recorded at Lingwood in Norfolk on June 28.

There have been 33 days so far this year when temperatures have exceeded 30C somewhere in the UK.



The record is 34 days in 1995, so that record is likely to be broken next week.

Deputy chief forecaster Mike Silverstone said: “Temperatures will climb through the weekend and, more significantly, through much of next week.

“After a brief dip on Monday, high pressure will move across the UK before settling to the east, allowing a southerly flow to develop.

“A fairly widespread heatwave is likely across large parts of England and Wales, with hot conditions developing in places.

“The heat is expected to peak for much of England, Wales, Northern Ireland and Scotland on Wednesday, with up to 34C possible in parts of central and southern England and south-east Wales.



“East Anglia and south-east England, however, could see temperatures even higher on Thursday.

“Humidity levels are also expected to increase through the week, which may make conditions feel more uncomfortable, particularly overnight.”

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has issued yellow heat health alerts for the East Midlands, West Midlands, South East, South West, East of England, Yorkshire and the Humber, and London.



They will come into force at 9am on Saturday and end at 9pm on Tuesday.

Last month was the driest July for England and Wales since records began in 1836, according to provisional figures released by the Met Office.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Nineteen counties across England recorded effectively no rainfall – 1mm or less – across the whole of the month, Met Office figures show.

The UK, England and Wales have all recorded their sunniest July on record – and for England and Wales it was the sunniest calendar month ever observed, the Met Office said.

News.title: Eerie video shows water in giant 18ft-deep well MOVING in earthquake hotspot where 20,000 died – and no one knows why
News.content:
AN eerie video shows water in an 18ft-deep well moving in an earthquake hotspot where 20,000 people died, leaving locals baffled.

Residents in an Indian village have been left scratching their heads for an answer after the well has been “shaking” continuously for days.



Footage posted on social media shows the water rippling and surging inside the well, located in the Morbi district in the western Indian state of Gujarat.

Locals fear an earthquake could be on its way.



The region suffered one of the world’s worst earthquakes in 2001, which left at least 20,00 dead.

The 18-foot-deep well is built on the farmland of Pranjivan Sadariya in Virparda village.



“When I arrived at my farm on Sunday, water from the well was spilling over the edge, and the same thing has continued ever since,” Mr Sadariya said, adding that the well was built only three months ago.

Officials have ruled out an earthquake or tectonic activity as the cause of the bizarre phenomenon and launched an investigation.



The Institute of Seismological Research in the state’s Gandhinagar, which reportedly found no seismic event and no active fault line linked to the phenomenon.

Experts have been roped in to investigate whether the shape and depth of the well could be amplifying the movement – a phenomenon known as a “well seiche” or resonance, in which water oscillates back and forth.

Morbi District Collector Swapnil Khare said a team of scientists would visit the site to investigate exactly what is happening underground.

Experts say such groundwater disturbances are unusual but can occur during periods of intense rainfall and rapid aquifer recharge – the process where water moves down from the land surface to replenish underground water reserves.

District geologist JS Vadher said there was no evidence of seismic activity and suggested the strange movement was linked to heavy monsoon rain and groundwater recharge.



“This is not seismic activity. Prima facie, it appears that following heavy upstream rainfall, groundwater is recharging and air trapped in the pore spaces of rocks is being released, causing the disturbance in the well,” Vadher explained.

India has been witnessing heavy monsoon rains with several regions submerged in flood waters leaving thousands displaced and more than 1,00 killed.

The earthquake in 2001 struck on January 26 at 8.46am and hit with a magnitude of 7.6.

As well as killing more than 20,000 people a further 166,000 were injured and some 400,000 buildings were destroyed.

Both Gujarat in India and the Pakistani province of Sindh were affected.

News.title: Murderer caught on pet cam brutally killing sister's boyfriend in row over dogs
News.content:
Murderer caught on pet cam brutally killing sister's boyfriend in row over dogs

Anthony Junior Murray used a combat knife to attack Joe Burton on New Year's Eve at the killer's flat in Bury, Greater Manchester

View 3 Images Anthony Junior Murray stabbed Joe Burton with a combat knife (Image: GMP)

A murderer who plunged a knife into the back of his sister's boyfriend after a row over a dog was caught in the act on a pet camera.

‌



Anthony Junior Murray, 25, stabbed Joe Burton, 23, with a combat knife on New Year's Eve then told police he was "not aware of the happenings" in an attempt to cover his crimes. But he was caught out when it emerged the attack had been filmed by a camera installed in his flat.

‌



The incident took place at 11.49pm on December 31 last year at a flat on Tarn Drive in Bury, Greater Manchester. Minshull Street Crown Court heard that Murray's sister, Kayleigh, had been in an on-off relationship with Mr Burton but this was "sadly blighted by alcohol abuse on both sides", prosecutor Rob Hall told Murray's trial.

‌



Although the pair had a child together in 2024, their "issues with alcohol continued". Murray invited his sister to the flat, who arrived with Mr Burton.

View 3 Images Joe Burton was stabbed in the back (Image: MEN Media)

Mr Hall told the trial, which concluded last month: "On the evening of New Year's Eve 2025, a time that should have been about socialising and welcoming in 2026, in a first floor flat in Bury, this defendant, Anthony Junior Murray, 25, lost his temper and stabbed Joe Burton, 23, the boyfriend of the defendant’s sister, to death.

‌



"He did that with a combat knife that he owned. The one stab wound that was inflicted with that knife was to Joe Burton’s left upper back area. The stab wound penetrated to a depth of approximately 18cm, which is almost to the full extent of the blade of that knife."

Manchester Evening News reports that Murray lived alone in his flat with his two dogs called Zarla and Beau Beau. He installed a camera in the flat to monitor the pets.

On New Year's Eve, Kayleigh is understood to have been "particularly intoxicated" and "appeared to be struggling to stand," the court heard. After the four let off some fireworks, "tensions started to rise".

‌



Mr Hall told the court: "There are a number of things in the mix by this stage, intoxication, lateness of the hour, the state of Kayleigh Murray and the tensions between the Murray family and Joe Burton." Before the stabbing, Murray and Mr Burton had been fighting over the dogs.

Mr Burton said: "F*** off dog, doing my head in." Later he said: "Shut up Beau I’ve had enough of you." Murray said: "What do you want me to do, put my dogs in a cage for you?"

"No I don’t," Mr Burton replied. "What do you want me to do, you f****** idiot," Murray replied. He continued: "Get the f*** out of my house kn******, why should I have to cage my dogs because of you?"

‌



He continued: "I don’t give a f***, I never trusted you from day one. I never trusted you. Why is Kayleigh like that? It has always been about you." Murray told Mr Burton "I’ll slit your f****** throat".

Mr Burton said: "I haven’t done anything wrong Anthony." A "struggle followed, after which Murray stabbed Mr Burton once to the back.

View 3 Images Police at the scene of the stabbing on Tarn Drive in Bury (Image: MEN Media)

‌



His reaction was "Not to help Joe Burton or call 999" but to call his family instead, being "selective" in telling his father, Anthony Senior, and his siblings about what he had done. The selective story telling then turned into a series of lies once officers arrived to the scene, the court heard.

A call to 999 was made by Kayleigh "out of concern for him [Murray]", with his family then driving to the flat and arriving moments before the police. At 12.07am, Murray claimed that "another person had stabbed" Mr Burton, later saying he had "been out all day" at the Bridge Tavern pub in nearby Radcliffe before coming home to find Mr Burton "bleeding to death".

In a later account, Murray said he didn't know who had been stabbed, claiming it may be to do with issues he had previously had with his downstairs neighbours. Murray was arrested at 12.30am, while Mr Burton was pronounced dead at 12.43am.

‌



In a written statement the next day, Murray accepted he had present at the flat and that a "fight" had started between Mr Burton and a man he didn't wish to name. He claimed he tried to intervene but left the flat, finding Mr Burton injured upon his return.

In a second statement, he accepted that the knife used in the stabbing belonged to him. Mr Hall told the court the attack was captured on the dog camera in a "remarkable stroke of luck".

When he was played the footage in a police interview, Murray said: "I cannot give an account of what went on in the footage or what I was thinking at the time as I blanked this out and I am not aware of the happenings." He said his previous statements represented his memory of what happened that night.

‌



During the trial, Murray, of Tarn Drive, Bury, claimed he acted in self-defence and didn't mean to stab Mr Burton. Today, he was ordered to serve a minimum of 18 years behind bars before he can be considered for parole.

Sentencing, Judge Maurice Greene told Murray: "It is not my task to put a value on Joe Burton’s life because no sentence can do that. Criminal law can not restore him to his family. But the court must recognise the seriousness of the harm caused, and I do."

Mr Hall said: "The Crown says that Mr Murray’s actions and the lies after the stabbing are the clearest evidence that he knew only too well what he had done and the seriousness of the consequences for him if that was discovered." Jurors found Murray guilty of murder by a majority of 11 to one after eight hours of deliberations.

Article continues below

Defending, Bernard Richmond KC paid tribute to the "quiet dignity" displayed by Mr Burton’s family during the case. Mr Richmond said that Murray recognised that the "life sentence he knows you are going to pass is not just a life sentence on him, but a life sentence on all of those who have been affected by this".

He said that the single blow inflicted by Murray was "horrific", but pointed out it was one blow and was not a more sustained attack. Mr Richmond said Murray’s lies "do him no credit" but that "none of them stand scrutiny at all".

News.title: Hundreds of children hold emotional vigil in Hornsea for teenage boy who drowned
News.content:
Hundreds of children hold emotional vigil in Hornsea for teenage boy who drowned

Emergency services scrambled to South Promenade in Hornsea, East Yorkshire., at around 6pm on Tuesday after reports of a concern for safety of a teenage boy in the water

View 4 Images A heartbreaking tribute to a teenager who drowned in the sea at Hornsea

Hundreds of children gathered in Hornsea to hold a vigil for a teenage boy who died after being swept out to sea while playing with his pals.

‌



The teen got in trouble in the rough seas just 11 minutes after the lifeguards clocked off, it is said. Emergency services scoured the coast just off Hornsea, East Yorkshire, before the 13-year-old boy’s body was eventually pulled from the water in the early hours of Wednesday morning.

‌



On Friday afternoon, his friends gathered to pay their respects to the teenager outside his school, Sirius West in Hull, East Yorkshire. Traffic stopped as the children wandered into the road and released scores of balloons.

‌



A teacher there said: “It is very sad. The school have got their own tribute inside the gates. I am sure something else will be going up. He has been here a while. He was a lovely, lovely lad. A really nice kid. It is shame these things happen.”

View 4 Images The 13-year-old boy apparently got in trouble minutes after the lifeguards had finished for the day (Image: Kevin Allitt/PA Wire)

Another parent said: “The boy who passed away, my daughter is in his sister’s class. I think it was lovely. It is a massive thing to come and pay their respect. He is from Africa."

‌



The parent said his sister is crying for her friend, adding: "You are never ready for anything like this. Most of it has been done by the kids who organised it.” A teddy bear tribute had been left attached to the school fence saying "Forever 13".

After the teen's body was recovered, Chief Superintendent Phil Booker, of Humberside Police, said: "This is an incredibly heartbreaking outcome, and our thoughts are with the boy’s family and friends at this devastating time."

View 4 Images A massive multi-agency search was launched after the boy went missing (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

‌



He said emergency services were called to the South Promenade in Hornsea shortly after 6pm on Tuesday "following reports of a concern for safety involving a 13-year-old boy who had got into difficulty whilst swimming in the water. “An extensive search operation was launched involving specialist Humberside search officers including our Marine Unit and drone pilots, alongside HM Coastguard, Yorkshire Ambulance Service, and Humberside Fire and Rescue Service. Tragically, at around 4.30am Wednesday, 5 August, a body was recovered from the water.

"His death is not being treated as suspicious, and a file will now be prepared for the Coroner. “We know the sadness and concern this will cause in the community, and we would ask that the family’s privacy is respected during this incredibly difficult time. I would like to thank all of the emergency services involved in the search, along with members of the public for their support and cooperation."

View 4 Images The scene at South Promenade in Hornsea (Image: Kevin Allitt/PA Wire)

‌



At least 40 people have lost their lives in water-related incidents since May 24. The Mirror has been running a water safety campaign after a horrifying spate of drownings in the early heatwaves. Save Lives for Sam has been backed by the RNLI and Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who are warning the public to take care in the water.

Withernsea Town Council has sent its deepest condolences to the people of Hornsea following the latest tragedy, the death of the teenager who police have not yet formally identified.

In a letter to Hornsea Town Council, Withernsea’s deputy mayor Sharon Carman said the two coastal communities shared a particular bond, strengthened by their recent experiences of tragedy and loss.

Article continues below

The letter said: “Withernsea Town Council wishes to express its deepest sympathy following the tragic incident in Hornsea. Our own community has only recently experienced profound loss on our shoreline and we understand the shock, sadness and collective grief that follow such events.

“Coastal communities share a particular bond. Shaped by the sea, strengthened in adversity and held together by the compassion of our residents. In moments like these, that connection feels especially strong.

“We stand with Hornsea’s community, its emergency responders and everyone affected. Please accept our heartfelt condolences and know that Withernsea is thinking of Hornsea at this very difficult time. We are all united by the grief these incidents create and thank them kindly for their thoughtfulness.”

News.title: South West Water announces strict hosepipe ban for millions across five areas
News.content:
South West Water announces strict hosepipe ban for millions across five areas

South West Water says restrictions will come into force from 12.01am on Saturday for all customers across Devon, Cornwall, parts of Dorset and Somerset, and the Isles of Scilly

View 2 Images South West Water has asked people to stop using hosepipes (Image: Getty Images)

A new hosepipe ban has been announced as Britain continues to be gripped by dry weather – with a fresh heatwave set to strike in days.

‌



South West Water has confirmed temporary restrictions will be in place again from 12.01am on Saturday for all customers across Devon, Cornwall, parts of Dorset and Somerset, and the Isles of Scilly. It had previously introduced a ban in July.

‌



The utility firm said the move follows significantly below-average rainfall, prolonged dry weather and soaring demand, which have piled pressure on water supplies.

‌



The announcement comes as the Met Office warns temperatures are set to climb steadily next week, with a "fairly widespread heatwave" likely across large swathes of England and Wales.

Forecasters say highs could reach 36C in parts of East Anglia and south-east England by Thursday, following a weekend of increasingly hot and sunny weather. Under the temporary restrictions, customers must not use hosepipes to water gardens, wash cars, clean patios, driveways, walls or windows, or fill paddling pools, swimming pools and hot tubs.

However, water can still be used as normal for drinking, cooking, washing and flushing toilets.

‌



South West Water urged customers to continue using water carefully during the drought to help safeguard the environment and water resources.

View 2 Images The ban will come into force in just hours (Image: Getty)

The company added that certain exemptions apply, including for customers on the Priority Services Register, Blue Badge holders and those on its WaterSure tariff. Although the ban does not officially come into force until Saturday, South West Water has urged customers to begin adhering to the measures straight away to help safeguard supplies.

‌



Sam Bottomley, South West Water's water services director, said introducing a hosepipe ban was never a decision taken "lightly".

He said: "After an extended period of exceptionally low rainfall, combined with sustained high demand during the warmer weather, our region's rivers and water resources are under significant pressure.

"Every litre saved now will help protect our rivers and water resources while drought conditions continue."

Article continues below

South West Water said the decision came off the back of one of the "driest periods in recent years", with rainfall across the South West remaining well below seasonal averages over many months.

It added that the Environment Agency had declared drought across more than half of England, including the South West.

The Met Office has also confirmed that July 2026 was the driest July for England and Wales since records began 190 years ago.

News.title: Blue Flag beach sewage crisis as HUNDREDS of tourists fall sick at some of UK's best beaches
News.content:
Blue Flag beach sewage crisis as HUNDREDS of tourists fall sick at some of UK's best beaches

EXCLUSIVE: New figures from Surfers Against Sewage revealed hundreds of people started feeling unwell after visiting Blue Flag UK beaches that have officially been rated the best in the country

View 6 Images Blue Flag beaches across the country have seen reports of sickness in 2026 (Image: PA)

Dozens of people have fallen ill at award-winning British Blue Flag beaches, new figures revealed, despite water quality being rated "excellent" by the Environment Agency and Natural Resources Wales this year.

‌



Marine conservation charity Surfers Against Sewage (SAS) received more than 700 reports of sickness across 406 areas, including some of the most picturesque beaches in the UK - among them beaches favoured by celebrities and former Prime Ministers. Many of them have been given top status as a Blue Flag location, meaning they have the highest water quality, minimal waste, good biodiversity, and are safe and accessible.

‌



But data reveals that some of them may also contain harmful pathogens, with visitors reporting falling unwell with gastrointestinal, ear, nose and throat, viral, respiratory and skin conditions.

‌



View 6 Images Croyde Bay had the most reports of any one beach in England (Image: Keep Britain Tidy / SWNS.com)

SAS revealed to the Mirror that it received 765 sickness reports across 406 locations in the UK in 2026 so far, with nearly half - 322 - coming in the months since May 1, as people flocked to the coast in the extreme heat. The majority of those reports came from Bournemouth, where 16 people said they fell unwell after visiting the coast.

Another 13 came from Croyde Bay in Croyde, North Devon, with Polzeath, the stunning stretch of sand in North Cornwall and the favourite of former PM David Cameron, coming third on the list.

‌



Cameron bought a £2million home near the beach, which he has been frequently pictured enjoying alongside his wife Samantha, in 2017. Polzeath was also one of the beaches where royals like Princes William and Harry grew up surfing, and other celebrities, including Coldplay frontman Chris Martin and renowned UK super chef Gordon Ramsay have made their homes there.

View 6 Images David and Samantha Cameron are fans of Polzeath (Image: PA)

But 13 people have reported feeling unwell after a trip to the beach this year so far, according to the SAS figures, and before visits reached their height in the middle of the summer holidays.

‌



Polzeath is followed by Rest Bay, in Porthcawl, in Bridgend, Wales, where 12 people said they were unwell after a visit to the beach. In Exmouth, the port town south of Exeter in Devon, another 10 people said they fell ill, with nine submitting reports in Portreath, another picturesque town on the north Cornwall coast.

Eight people said they were unwell after visiting Saunton Sands, a UNESCO-protected biosphere in North Devon's Braunton Burrows, Swanage Central in Dorset and Ogmore by Sea in Barry, Wales. Seven were recorded in Woolacombe Village, also in North Devon.

The hundreds of additional cases and their locations can be seen on the map below:

‌



The majority of those areas and beaches included in the top 10 SAS figures - six - are either areas with beaches that have been given Blue Flag awards, or beaches that have previously won the prize. For instance, in Bournemouth, from where 13 sickness reports were submitted, three came from Durley Chine beach, which won the prize in 2026.

The ones in the top 10 that didn't win the prize this year, Portreath, Saunton Sands and Woolacombe Village, were still in sparkling condition, according to the Environment Agency. Each of the trio were rated as having "excellent" quality of water in its latest ratings, which were handed down in 2025.

‌



The outlier among the group was Ogmore-by-Sea in Barry, which according to Natural Resources Wales, had "failed to meet water quality standards in the past few years".

Bathing quality ratings across the UK can be seen on the map below:

‌



While the service said it was not sure why water quality has consistently dipped in the area, it said storm overflows and drainage, ageing infrastructure, road and urban pollution, misconnected pipes and farmland pollution could play a role. There is no indication what could be behind sickness at the Blue Flag locations, but sewage dumping by water companies, the SAS says, is "making us sick".

Jo Morley, Head of Campaigns at SAS said in a statement to the Mirror: "Sewage dumping by water companies is making us sick. It has been for decades.

"Thousands of water users are reporting this to us, and this is likely just the tip of the iceberg. From gastroenteritis and ear infections, to weeks off work and hospitalisations. This is a public health crisis. We know that sewage is pouring into our waters, even during this summer's exceptionally dry weather, and it's totally unacceptable that people are getting ill in any case, especially after using bathing waters rated as 'excellent.'"

‌



View 6 Images Surfers Against Sewage are campaigning to end water privatisation in the UK (Image: PA)

"Our sickness reports are the only data showing the scale of sickness from sewage. There is no official Government data, and no legal protections for people using the water.

"This is symptomatic of a totally broken system that has put profits first for too long, allowing polluters to cash in in whilst dumping sewage without punishment, and this has to change. We should not have to worry about getting sick before diving in, any time of year, especially the summer.

‌



"If you're heading to the beach or your local swim spot, make sure you check the Safer Seas and Rivers Service for pollution alerts."

View 6 Images Thousands of Brits have flocked to beaches across the country during a record-breaking hot summer (Image: Getty Images)

SAS has received thousands of sickness reports since 2019, when it started recording, with a total of 8,313 in the last seven years. Most of those cases have come from Exmouth, which recorded 203, with Hove recording 140, Polzeath 117, Harlyn Bay 101, Westward Ho! 98, Tankerton 94, Gyllyngvase 85, Shoreham Beach 82, Worthing 78, and Summerleaze, for which 76 were recorded.

‌



SAS has urged Brits to use its Safer Seas and River Service to check for real-time pollution alerts if they head to the coast this summer.

View 6 Images Hundreds of reports came as people tried to cool off for the summer this year, and before the summer holidays (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

The charity hosts the service both on its website and via its own app, via which it tells people to report whether they become unwell after using UK water. The charity has also urged the Government to end privatisation in the water industry, and has championed the Clean Water Act as a path forward for the industry that protects both public health and the environment.

‌



It urged Prime Minister Andy Burnham to take control of failing water companies, remove their profit motive and pursue restructuring, starting with Thames Water.

The Mirror has contacted Keep England Clean and Keep Wales Clean, which administer the Blue Flag Awards to beaches in England and Wales. An Environment Agency spokesperson said: "We urge members of the public to follow UKHSA advice on swimming safely and to check Swimfo before visiting any of the country's 464 designated bathing waters.

"There are a range of sources of bacteria in our rivers, lakes and seas. These can include runoff from fields containing farm animals, as well as sewage treatment works and storm overflows, particularly following periods of heavy rainfall. Some bacteria can make people unwell."

‌



"Our waters are also home to a wide variety of wildlife, including birds and other animals, which naturally contribute bacteria to the environment and can affect water quality." A Natural Resources Wales spokesperson said: “We want people to enjoy Wales’ rivers, lakes and coastlines safely this summer.

"We monitor water quality at Wales' designated bathing waters throughout the bathing season, with results published online to help people make informed decisions about where and when to enter the water. Anyone who sees potential pollution should report it directly to us on 03000 65 3000 or online at naturalresources.wales/reportit, so our officers can respond.

“Natural water bodies can contain bacteria and other contaminants from a range of sources that are not always visible and can sometimes cause illness. We investigate reports of suspected pollution affecting rivers, lakes and coastal waters and work with partners, including water companies and local authorities, to establish the cause of incidents.

Article continues below

"Where there is evidence of environmental harm or breaches of environmental legislation, we take appropriate regulatory action. We encourage people to take sensible precautions when using open water, including avoiding swallowing water, washing or sanitising hands before eating, and seeking medical advice if they feel unwell after water activities. You can find advice here: Staying safe in outdoor water in Wales - Public Health Wales”

News.title: Katie Price fears son Harvey will have a heart attack after reaching 30 stone
News.content:
Katie Price fears son Harvey will have a heart attack after reaching 30 stone

Katie Price has shared her fears for her oldest child, Harvey, 24, who has Prader-Willi syndrome, which causes a constant hunger that can lead to severe obesity.

View 3 Images Katie Price says she's worried sick over her son, Harvey

Katie Price has said she fears her son Harvey will suffer a heart attack, explaining that he now weighs just under 30 stone.

‌



Harvey, who is Katie's oldest child, has the rare genetic condition Prader-Willi syndrome, which causes a constant hunger that can lead to severe obesity. He also autistic and blind.

‌



Speaking on Andrew Gold's Heretics podcast, Katie said: "I’m not worried about his eyesight. What I’m worried about is him having a heart attack, his obesity. He weighs just under 30 stone."

‌



She said it was "heartbreaking" to see him try and get in and out of the bath and said she had tried to put Harvey on Mounjaro, a diabetic drug being used for weight loss.

View 3 Images Katie Price said her son Harvey doesn't want to walk anywhere (Image: officialjunior_andre/ Instagram)

She said: “I’ve tried going private with him to start him on Mounjaro, but because of his medical… it’s easy for me to just give it, but because of his other medication, you have to have all the team tick it off."

‌



Revealing her son was now at "high risk of having a heart attack", she added: “It’s getting to a point now, where he doesn’t want to walk anywhere, he gets out of breath and sweats and they have said he is at high risk of having a heart attack.

“You try to [force him to walk] but he literally breaks into a sweat. I bath him twice a day and it breaks my heart seeing him get in and out of the bath because he’s so big and heavy."

Harvey, who has a legion of fans, is renowned for his uncensored comments. Explaining that he will make fun of himself, Katie shared: “He goes: ‘I’m like a humpback whale’, and I’m like: 'No you’re not Harv, I love you’.”

‌



View 3 Images Katie Price says son Harvey is at 'high risk of having a heart attack' (Image: officialjunior_andre/Instagram)

Katie was then asked if her son ever gets upset over his weight. However, she replied: “No. He says he’s got Santa’s belly, he’s all about Christmas now. “It’s funny, if he sees someone with a big belly, he goes ‘you’re a fat pepper pig’, randomly in the shops.

“He just comes out with it and I go: 'Harv, you mustn’t say that’ and he goes ‘sorry, d***head’, and I’m like ‘Harv, you mustn’t call them a d***head’.”

‌



With heartbreaking honesty, the star then revealed the things she has to do for her beloved son, who she admitted was a "baby in a man's body".

Revealing she is responsible for Harvey's hygiene, she shared: "He’s 24 and he’s a baby, he doesn’t know about hygiene, he’s on medication four times a day and he’ll die if he doesn’t have it.

“I have to bath him or wash him because he doesn’t understand. When I go to the toilet I have to wipe his bum, he wets the bed, he’s a baby in a man’s body."

Article continues below

News.title: Taiwan's president evacuated in dramatic war drill as Chinese battleships circle country
News.content:
Taiwan's president evacuated in dramatic war drill as Chinese battleships circle country

President William Lai sped off in an armoured vehicle as part of 10 days of military drills in Taiwan

View 3 Images Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te was taken to a secret command post in an armoured car (Image: Presidential Office of Taiwan/AFP via Getty Images)

Taiwan's president has been practising his escape route amid fears of a possible Chinese invasion.

‌



As part of ramped-up military drills, president William Lai sped off in an armoured vehicle in the middle of the night. The operation is part of the annual "Han Kuang" military drills taking place between August 5 and 15.

‌



It comes after 14 Chinese aircrafts and nine warships circled Taiwan on Wednesday, according to authorities. This comes as China has made numerous threats to take over the democratic island located to its southeast as Chinese president Xi Jinping claims Taiwan is part of his Communist empire.

‌



View 3 Images Taiwanese soldiers set up anti-tank obstacles on the Danjiang (Tamkang) Bridge to simulate stopping Chinese forces from approaching (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

This is the first time that President Lai took part in the Wan Chun plan since he took office in 2024, Taipei Times reports. US president Donald Trump explained in May that he wanted China and Taiwan to "cool down" as the US is "not looking for" travelling to Asia for a war.

‌



Asked if America would step in if a Chinese invasion was to happen in Taiwan, he said: "We’re supposed to travel 9,500 miles (15,289km) to fight a war. I’m not looking for that. I want them to cool down. I want China to cool down.

"We’re not looking to have wars, and if you kept it the way it is, I think China’s going to be okay with that." In response, Taiwan's foreign ministry said: "Taiwan is a sovereign and independent democratic nation and is not subordinate to the People’s Republic of China."

View 3 Images Taiwanese military deploys the Patriot surface-to-air missile systems at a riverside park to simulate a response to China's attacks (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Article continues below

Yesterday's drills featured exercises across Taiwan including coastal defences, logistics procedures, road barrier deployment drills and tactical training. The Presidential Office released images of Lai wearing body armour and a helmet and entering the back of an armoured vehicle.

The officials "conducted drills on commanding defensive operations and maintaining the continued functioning of government during emergency situations," office spokeswoman Karen Kuo said in a statement. The exercises aim to review the command structure and emergency response to ensure an effective operation in the event of "unforeseen circumstances", Kuo added.

Lai also watched missile launchers being fitted on one of the Coast Guard Administration's catamarans and learned about mine deployment operations.

News.title: Prince Harry 'determined for family reconciliation and won't do anything to jeopardise it'
News.content:
Prince Harry 'determined for family reconciliation and won't do anything to jeopardise it'

EXCLUSIVE: With Prince Harry hoping to reunite publicly with his once-estranged father the King at the Invictus Games in Birmingham, there is growing belief the Duke is placing a far greater importance on repairing damaged family ties

View 5 Images Prince Harry on his recent trip to the UK (Image: Wiktor Szymanowicz/Future Publishing via Getty Images)

Prince Harry is determined to reconcile with his family and won’t do anything to jeopardise it, according to a source.

‌



There is a growing belief that the Duke of Sussex is placing far greater importance on repairing family ties than at any point since he and his wife Meghan stepped back as working royals in 2020. He has been buoyed by his recent meeting with his once estranged father the King, which took place last month at Highgrove, alongside Meghan and their two children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet.

‌



And as the Mirror revealed earlier this week, Harry is hoping to appear publicly with Charles at next year's Invictus Games in Birmingham, with the organisers planning to invite the King to take part in either the opening or closing ceremony as well as visiting a range of sporting events to meet competitors.

‌



Prince Harry hopes to convince King Charles to join him at UK Invictus Games READ MORE :

View 5 Images Harry and his father at the opening of the Invictus Games in London in 2014 (Image: Getty Images)

Many see the key to full reconciliation between the Sussexes and the King as being that whatever happens in such meetings between them remains private.

No details have emerged about what happened at the meeting and in a recent string of photos shared by Meghan on Instagram of the family’s time in the UK last month, none included the King or Queen Camilla.

‌



A royal source said: "There's no doubt he [Harry] enjoyed his time in the UK with his family, especially getting the opportunity to see his father with his wife and children.

"The last few years have been incredibly emotional for him, and now he's reached a place where he wants to not only visit his home country more, but also would really like to be with his family. If the King were to attend the Invictus Games next year, and appear in public with him, it would be a huge moment for all of them.

View 5 Images The King on a walkabout in Dingwall in Scotland today (Image: Ewen Weatherspoon/PA Wire)

‌



"He wants the Birmingham Games to be the best ever, and it would be extra special to have all his family by his side, and that means the King as well.

"He's said before that he would like reconciliation with his family, so undoubtedly he's determined to make things work, and that means not doing anything to jeopardise that."

It is understood Harry wants to arrange further meetings with his father to also allow him to spend time with his grandchildren, who he has hardly seen since he and Meghan quit their royal roles in 2020 and moved to the United States.

‌



And the Duke is to continue his controversial campaign demanding taxpayer-funded security - paving the way for future visits with his family - after previously saying without it, it was too dangerous to bring his wife and children to the UK.

View 5 Images Harry and Meghan with their children Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet (Image: @meghan/Instagram)

The source added: “[The duke] is not going to give up pursuing the security avenue because that would guarantee Meghan and the children coming over with him, and alleviate a lot of the stress he is under when it comes to arranging such a trip.”

‌



However, whether Buckingham Palace believes the timing is right for a public reunion between father and son is another question altogether.

The Sussexes have been estranged from the royals after Harry criticised his father, stepmother Camilla, brother the Prince of Wales and sister-in-law Kate in his Oprah interview, Netflix documentary, interviews and his autobiography Spare, after stepping down from the working monarchy six years ago.

View 5 Images The King with his two sons at the 2014 Games (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Royal expert and former BBC royal correspondent Jennie Bond told the Mirror: “It will all depend on whether the Palace feels Harry and Meghan are to be trusted.

“So there are a lot of ifs and buts at this point. However, there would be a wonderful symmetry if Charles, Camilla and William were alongside Harry for the opening of the Birmingham games – just as they were at the inaugural games in 2014 in London.

“I think there is a fighting chance that the King will be there. It’s such a brilliant cause and probably Harry's best achievement. I’m sure Charles is proud of his son.”

‌



While the King appears prepared to keep lines of communication open, there is little indication that the Prince and Princess of Wales share the same outlook.

William's relationship with his brother remains deeply fractured, and there is no expectation inside royal circles that Harry will be welcomed back into the wider family in any meaningful way yet.

Article continues below

And Jennie added: “As for William, there are no signs yet of any thaw in the frost. But he has much to think about with the 30th anniversary of Diana’s death next year, which — before the rift – is something he would have marked with Harry, as well as the Invictus Games.

“Personally, I think it would be brilliant if we could see them all standing alongside one another and calling a halt to the bitterness. Families are complicated. Families fall out. But that doesn’t mean it has to last forever.”

News.title: 'I've endured life-changing injuries for 16 years after gang members got wrong house and shot me - I want justice'
News.content:
'I've endured life-changing injuries for 16 years after gang members got wrong house and shot me - I want justice'

WARNING - GRAPHIC IMAGE: Jason Franklin was watching From Paris with Love with his partner at their home in Bristol when intruders opened fire and shot him

View 6 Images Jason Franklin had been enjoying a quiet night when he was shot in the head (Image: Jason Franklin / SWNS)

A dad was left with gruesome injuries after he was shot in the head by gang members who got the wrong house.

‌



Jason Franklin, 42, had been enjoying a quiet night in with his partner Keela, 36, and their son Lucas, then just five months old, when intruders attempted to break down their front door before shooting him through the glass door panel.

‌



The dad-of-four from Bristol, was left with a hole in his head and shards of glass in his eyes, and still has more than 100 pieces of shrapnel in his forehead. It is said police told Jason he had got caught in the crossfire of a war between rival gangs, who had mistakenly turned up at his property, thinking it belonged to someone else.

‌



View 6 Images Jason was shot in the head (Image: Jason Franklin / SWNS)

The fencer, who has since not able to work due to mental health struggles, said: "I'm devastated that the people who did this to me were never caught. The lasting damage that it's had on my mental health has been horrible.

"I think it's terrible that there's been no repercussions at all. I've got PTSD, anxiety, depression; it's really affected Lucas as I wasn't able to take him out to places when he was growing up, due to my mental health. We've not been able to live like a normal family."

‌



On the evening of Sunday, April 4, 2010, Jason and Keela were snuggled up on the sofa, in their home in Bristol, watching From Paris with Love, whilst Lucas, now 16, slept in the pram next to them. It was Easter Sunday, and Jason, who usually went to bed early, had decided to stay up later than usual, as he had the bank holiday Monday off work.

View 6 Images Jason was attacked after thugs mistakenly targeted the wrong house (Image: Jason Franklin / SWNS)

At around 10 pm, Keela went upstairs to put Lucas in his cot, before returning downstairs, whilst Jason drifted in and out of sleep on the sofa. Half an hour later, Jason was woken up with a start, at the sound of a banging noise.

‌



"It sounded like someone was kicking the door down", he said. Confused, Jason raced to the front door and pressed his body against it to try and stop the intruders from entering the property.

"I had no idea whatsoever who it could be", he said. "I was so scared, I didn't know why anyone would want to try and break into my house."

View 6 Images Jason, pictured with his family, was left with a hole in his head (Image: Jason Franklin / SWNS)

‌



Suddenly, there was a loud bang, and a smell of smoke. The glass panels in the front door had been shattered by a bullet, which hit Jason in the top of the head.

"The intruders couldn't get through the door, so they decided to just shoot through the glass", Jason said. "Weirdly, I wasn't in any pain at all".

Jason's head began to pour with blood, and he raced upstairs to grab a towel to press onto his head, leaving bloody handprints all over the walls. Keela immediately called 999, and the intruders ran away from the property.

‌



Jason was rushed to the hospital, where he had 10 stitches to close up the wound, and an operation to remove shards of glass from the front door from his eyes. "When they shot me in the head, it damaged the nerve, so I couldn't feel much, but my eyes were in so much pain", he said.

View 6 Images Jason has dealt with mental health struggles since the shooting (Image: Jason Franklin / SWNS)

Police investigating the shooting told Jason and Keela that the attackers had used a homemade bullet, which had shattered on impact, leaving Jason with 100 pieces of shrapnel in his forehead.

‌



"Doctors said it would make the scarring worse if they tried to take them out", Jason said. "You can still feel little bits of metal if you touch my head in certain places."

Police explained that they believed the attack was part of a dispute between rival gangs, who had got the wrong house, and mistakenly shot Jason.

"They (the gang members) didn't do their research; they were just told to go to the house next to the boarded-up house, but they got the wrong side", he said.

‌



After five days, Jason was discharged from the hospital and went to stay at his mum's house, where Keela and Lucas were already staying.

View 6 Images Jason was left with 100 pieces of shrapnel in his forehead (Image: Jason Franklin / SWNS)

"Mum lived down the road, literally four doors down from where the shooting happened, so it was really scary going back there", Jason said. "I was scared that something else could happen to me or my family".

Article continues below

Two months later, the family moved into a two-bed flat on the other side of Bristol, which helped them to feel much safer. However, by the end of the year, the police had closed the case, as they had exhausted all lines of enquiry, leaving Jason devastated.

The dad of four's mental health has been extremely badly affected by the random attack, and in the years after, Jason struggled to leave the house because of his PTSD. "I'm still unwell to this day; sometimes I struggle to play with my sons and take them out to certain places", he said.

The Mirror has contacted Avon and Somerset Police for comment.

News.title: How police left a registered sex offender free to murder and attack women
News.content:
His first victim was attacked was on a busy Tube in central London.

Levy boarded and positioned himself directly in front of the woman, before leaning his elbow on her. She moved away.

A few minutes later, she felt something touch her, over her clothes, on her vagina. Such was the force Levy used, that she felt like it was an attempt to push his fingers inside her through clothing.

She grabbed Levy's hand and asked what he was doing, but he did not respond.

When other passengers asked if she was all right, Levy protested his innocence.

"What are you talking about - look my hand is covered," he said, pointing to the jumper draped over his arm.

Levy then called her "crazy" and "stupid" and got off the tube at Westminster station.

The woman got off at the next stop, upset and crying.

She went on to report the assault to BTP. There was CCTV available of Levy, but police did not identify him. He would only be linked to the case two years later, after more women had been attacked.

A year after his first Tube assault, he assaulted three more women in quick succession and was arrested.

After being assaulted herself, the first of those three victims then filmed Levy sexually assaulting a second, unidentified woman, travelling in the same carriage.

The first woman immediately reported what had happened to BTP and provided the footage. Levy assaulted a third woman a week later.

After he had been questioned and had denied the three offences, BTP officers said they did not have enough evidence to charge, and he was released on bail.

The subsequent BTP investigation was full of delays. It was weeks before identity parades were arranged, and BTP did not approach the CPS for six months.

When it did, in May 2025, a CPS team had to scramble to make an emergency charging decision overnight, because BTP had again arrested Levy and wanted him in court the next day. This was highly unusual - BTP had known about the initial offences for six months.

In a statement, BTP Assistant Chief Constable Charlie Doyle said: "It is clear that opportunities to expedite the investigation were missed and we have amended our procedures to address these issues to ensure that repeat offenders are dealt with expeditiously and that linked offences are prioritised more effectively."

News.title: Serial sex offender guilty of murdering two women and raping third
News.content:
Earlier this year, Levy, 40, was found guilty by a jury at Inner London Crown Court of groping 10 women on the Tube and an 11th while in prison.

Details of this trial can now be reported after his conviction at the Old Bailey.

The offences took place between April 2022 at the prison, followed by the Tube assaults between 24 October 2023 and May 2025.

He had already been convicted of sexually assaulting two women in 2018, which was why he was in prison in 2022.

The sex offender had lost sight in one eye in an attack in May 2024 and played on this, claiming that his partial sight made him unsteady on his feet and all contact was accidental on these crowded trains.

Levy's tactic was to tie a jumper or hoodie around his waist, strap his arm down, and then back towards his victim with his hand fully or partially covered so he could grope them.

One of the Tube assault victims told the court: "It wasn't long before I learned that my attacker was already known to the police for sexual violence and is a convicted sex offender.

"You could not begin to understand the horror I felt at hearing this.

"How could a male who does this so often and so brazenly be allowed to repeat his attacks?

"Knowing this made me feel even more unsafe, the possibility that I could encounter Simon Levy again made me fearful and the idea that he would harm more women and that there would be many more victims was unthinkable."

During a sentencing hearing in June for the Tube attacks, Judge Michael Evans told Levy : "You were on the Tube for one purpose only, to sexually assault women."

Levy was convicted of 11 counts of indecent assault, including grabbing the prison guard in 2022, and given an extended sentence consisting of a six-year jail term plus a three-year period on licence.
