Sports.title: Mexico and Argentina line up behind Infantino to deepen football’s civil war
Sports.content:
Mexico’s football federation has broken ranks with the rest of Concacaf by publicly backing the beleaguered Gianni Infantino in a move that has deepened world football’s civil war.

Concacaf has called for a thorough review of Fifa’s governance in the light of the World Cup sell-off debacle, and is backing Uefa’s demands for meaningful change, although has yet to follow its European counterparts by threatening to boycott tournaments if they do not achieve their objectives.

In a statement issued on Thursday night, the FMF went some way towards explaining Concacaf’s reticence, as its second-biggest member after the US was unequivocal in its support for the Fifa president. In a Fifa statement released under Infantino’s name on Wednesday, the world governing body had called for its institutional practices to be respected, a coded way of condemning any leadership challenge before next March’s scheduled presidential election, which the FMF endorsed.

“The Mexican Football Federation is convinced that football is its fundamental value and that its best defence lies in institutional integrity and respect for the governance and processes that safeguard it,” the FMF said. “Therefore, the FMF will not recognise or approve any process convened outside of this institutional framework, and it embraces the call issued by president Infantino on 5 August 2026 to collectively continue developing football for the benefit of its 211 member associations.

“The FMF supports president Infantino’s leadership in continuing to promote the development of football through institutional strengthening.”

The Argentina Football Association (AFA) followed Mexico’s lead by backing Infantino in a gushing tribute and expressing support for his leadership over the past decade. Unlike Concacaf, South America’s Conmebol appears united behind Infantino, while in an intriguing subplot there is growing speculation that Mexico would like to switch confederations to join the latter.

“In relation to the recent events that are public knowledge, we must recognise the decision of the administration to withdraw a project that generated, within the football family and from its inception, many more uncertainties than certainties,” the AFA statement read.

“That is why it is worth highlighting the acceptance of the errors made in this process and the apology expressed in the heartfelt message displayed to the 211 member associations of Fifa. Prioritising governance standards is a fundamental pillar for strengthening good relations between Fifa, its member associations and the confederations.

“In the same way, and as we have already expressed, you are leading a management that led to a profound transformation of Fifa, which opened the doors of the organisation to all member associations and confederations, so that with a frank and direct dialogue, we can, together, continue to promote football at all levels and disciplines.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“This transformation was based on a model of transparent governance, respect for statutory structures and the monitoring of democratic procedures, essential principles for the football family to be united, firm and working to continue generating improvements in sports and institutions, which have an impact on a better quality of life for millions of human beings who practise our beloved sport.

“Accordingly, with the upcoming Fifa congress approaching, the association that we proudly preside over firmly believes and reaffirms that the way forward is to continue to work under your leadership, so that we can continue to develop better and even more inclusive football.”

Earlier on Thursday, the Confederation of African Football had reaffirmed its support for Infantino, providing him with further allies as he fights to extend his 10-year reign.

Sports.title: Norway’s Klaveness tells Fifa president Infantino to resign: ‘There is no trust now’
Sports.content:
The Norwegian FA will ask Gianni Infantino to resign with immediate effect after his doomed attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Norway is the first federation to call directly for the Fifa president to step down after a series of controversies that came to a head with the crisis engulfing his Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme.

The decision was made at a meeting of the Norwegian Football Federation board (NFF) on Thursday night. Norway has consistently taken a lead in efforts to scrutinise Fifa’s governance and recent events have taken any faith in its leadership beyond the point of no return.

“We decided that there is no trust in Infantino now,” the NFF president, Lise Klaveness, told the Guardian. “We have been worried consistently and there has been one more step in a worrying direction every year, every part of the year. The trust is now gone for us, there is no way back for Infantino.

“We’re left in a very polarised cooperation globally and, I would say, chaos. So we will ask him to resign immediately so that the global football community can look ahead and cooperate going into the future.”

The NFF is expected to formally write a letter requesting Infantino’s resignation in the coming week. Norway was among a handful of countries not to back his re-election as president next March, although several European federations have withdrawn their endorsement in the past week.

“We understand that we’re one country, but it’s our position,” Klaveness said. “It’s just one step further for us. We did not vote for him in 2023 but we hoped we would support him, he was elected and the reason why we were so clear in our statements was to really give the signal that we wanted him to implement the good reforms he was part of. But he didn’t, and now we will ask him to resign.”

The NFF agreed to demand a full review into the package of reforms passed upon Infantino’s ascent to the presidency in 2016, which were intended to extricate Fifa from the corruption crisis that had previously dogged the governing body. Klaveness said the investigation should ask “what was implemented, what was not, what should have been implemented and what we should also implement to make this a functioning organisation”.

Norway will also formalise a fresh complaint to Fifa’s ethics committee on three fronts, taking in the FFE scandal, the award of Fifa’s peace prize to Donald Trump and the Folarin Balogun affair at the World Cup. It will attempt to bring a number of major European federations on board for its submission in an effort to further increase the pressure on Infantino.

“We want the ethics committee to show their work transparently because this is a very big part of the issue,” Klaveness said. “There are all kinds of control mechanisms in place but they are not really holding the council and president accountable.”

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino leaves after attending the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations match between Malawi and Zambia in Rabat. Photograph: AP

In June, the NFF wrote to the ethics committee supporting a complaint by the advocacy group FairSquare, which centred on alleged breaches of political neutrality by Infantino. It will now make a new submission that asks for the three situations to be considered individually. “We will join them in one letter but they are very different cases and we want the ethical committee to treat them separately,” Klaveness said.

The NFF is understood to have particular concerns that the timing of Infantino’s FFE offer, which promised federations significant financial gains if accepted, may constitute an abuse of position at this proximity to a presidential election. It has also been observed that the FFE scheme, had it been passed, would have locked in commitments extending well beyond Infantino’s term.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to The Recap The best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s action Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

As with its call for Infantino to step down, Norway is the first federation to adopt a public stance regarding the peace prize or the Balogun case. Fifa’s decision to suspend the USA striker’s red card during the World Cup, meaning he was free to face Belgium in the last 16, came after Trump had called Infantino to discuss the ban.

Uefa’s federations have stood together in backing a potential boycott of Fifa competitions, a stance Uefa reasserted on Thursday despite Infantino’s shelving of FFE. Klaveness said the move is not merely symbolic and is intended to bring swift results.

“There’s no point in Uefa standing in a war position for half a year,” she said. “That would not be good at all. Now it’s crucial that we do it because global football cooperation is at stake. It’s very good to see we have strong leadership in Uefa that knows now is crunch time for this case. We cannot sell out this core of football.”

The first competition in line for a boycott would be the Under-20 Women’s World Cup, which is due to start in Poland on 5 September, but Klaveness expects the continued turmoil to have been resolved by then.

“I hope and think it will not come to that,” she said. “A lot of water will go under the bridge before that. But this is why we ask Infantino to resign. It’s so unstable now that it’s a matter of time. He cannot recover this and we cannot put the sport on the spot. The biggest priority is to be together with Uefa and have this strong position.”

Klaveness and the NFF have held a consistent line in calling for scrutiny of Fifa’s operations since she assumed her position in March 2022. She has been vocal on human rights issues and governance standards within Fifa, criticising failings surrounding the Qatar World Cup and questioning the process that awarded Saudi Arabia the 2034 edition of the tournament.

Sports.title: England striker Ivan Toney charged with assault after Soho nightclub incident
Sports.content:
The England footballer Ivan Toney has been charged with assault after an incident at a nightclub in Soho in December last year.

Scotland Yard said the striker had been charged on 31 July with assault causing actual bodily harm. Toney, who plays for the Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli, is due to appear at Westminster magistrates court on 24 September.

The Sun newspaper reported in December that Toney had been arrested after an alleged head-butt. It claimed a fan recognised the footballer and grabbed at him while seeking a photograph with him before the incident.

On Friday the Metropolitan police said the charges related to an incident on 6 December at a nightclub on Wardour Street in central London, reportedly the now-closed 100 Wardour Street.

A spokesperson for Toney said: “Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court.”

Toney was at the centre of one of the most curious transfers on deadline day in August 2024 when he completed a late move from Brentford to Al-Ahli worth a reported £40m. He has also played for Newcastle United and his home town club Northampton Town, as well as several others on loan as he looked to establish himself.

Seen as a late bloomer in football terms, he had made only two Premier League appearances before his 25th birthday, but went on to score 67 goals in 128 appearances over the next three seasons at the top level.

He has played 10 times for England, scoring once in a friendly match against Belgium in 2024, and was part of the 2026 World Cup squad, making appearances against Argentina in the semi-final and in the win over France as England finished third.

Sports.title: Boardroom struggle deepens gloom as West Ham prepare for life on the outside
Sports.content:
There have been 10 summers of West Ham’s London Stadium tenancy and a number of winters of discontent. As the Hammers kick off the new season on Saturday, a Carabao Cup first-round fixture with Portsmouth is a stark reminder of reduced circumstances, further confirmation of last season’s relegation from the Premier League. The summer has been as bleak as any of those winters, with a number of factors colliding to deepen the gloom of relegation.

Certain clubs, including West Ham back in 2011-12 when promotion was achieved at first time of asking under Sam Allardyce, have used the Championship to take a beat, to refresh and replenish. Can this be the case at West Ham 2026? The Hammers are short-odds favourites for promotion but behind the scenes it has been a summer of turbulence, particularly in the boardroom, where a power struggle is being fought.

Portsmouth will bring 9,000 supporters on Saturday but will David Sullivan be present? This week it was revealed the operators of London Stadium had recommended the former joint-chair (but still co-owner) stay away, because of the “potential for demonstrations and anti-social behaviour by some spectators”.

It is expected that Sullivan will turn up, despite a fans’ advisory board statement that his attendance would cause “offence and upset”. It has been suggested that he wants to enjoy the coming season as a fan and is happy to bide his time before any consideration of selling his 38.8% stake. Considering his personal circumstances, his attendance would be a brazenly unpopular act. On 25 May, when relegation was confirmed despite a home win over Leeds, Sullivan was forced to leave the stadium early for his own safety.

View image in fullscreen Daniel Kretinsky wants to increase his shares in West Ham to just under 50.1%. Photograph: David W Černý/Reuters

Sullivan continues to deny allegations of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour towards women over several decades made by the BBC’s Panorama documentary in early June, though he stepped down from his role on the eve of the broadcast “to avoid disruption to the club while he addresses the matter privately”.

Even before those allegations became public, Sullivan was a lightning rod, lambasted for his stewardship of a club in vertiginous decline since winning the Europa Conference League in May 2023. The £100m fee received for Declan Rice that summer was frittered away. Fellow Prague hero Jarrod Bowen, the club captain, has pledged to stay on, tasked with leading the club back up.

Until his defenestration Sullivan had acted as the club’s de facto director of football, often to the frustration of those in the football department. His chief ally, Karren Brady, stepped down in April as storm clouds gathered, severing a working relationship that dated as far back as 1990.

Among the club’s support, 50,000 season tickets have been sold for the attempt at re-entry to the Premier League. The overriding desire among fans is for Sullivan to completely depart the scene. His announced departure had installed a modicum of optimism.

Potential new sheriffs are circling but the picture is complicated, any future direction opaque as a result. As Sullivan stepped down the expectation was that Daniel Kretinsky, the Czech billionaire owner of Royal Mail who has owned 27% of West Ham since 2021, would make his move. Instead, this week, he cut that share down to just under 25%, though this was part of a strategy.

Last weekend, the familiar face of Amanda Staveley entered the picture. In July 2024 she departed Newcastle, after her leading role in bringing in the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund, but now Staveley wants to return to football. Last September, she was linked with a takeover at Tottenham, and it is suggested she will use a similar source of funding to engineer her move for West Ham. Among Newcastle fans, with their club faltering this summer, Staveley’s energy is lamented. With her connections, some Hammers fan hope she could have a similar galvanising effect.

View image in fullscreen David Sullivan’s closet ally, Karren Brady, left the club in April. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy

The key is the 25% that belonged to the late David Gold, Sullivan’s former joint-chair. As Staveley loomed, Kretinsky appeared ready to take up his first refusal on purchasing that 25% from Vanessa Gold, David’s daughter and current co-chair. Adding that to his 27% would take him beyond 50.1%, leaving him liable for a formal takeover offer. But shifting 2% to a Czech ally, the entrepreneur Jakub Havrlant, now means he would be short of that obligation should he cut across Staveley’s ambitions by buying Gold’s stake. Sullivan’s shares also hold the balance of power and Staveley’s next move is keenly awaited.

While that plays out, what of football? The arrival of free agent, the former Brighton and Ajax defender, Joël Veltman, was the first addition of a summer where the sales of Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham and Crysencio Summerville to Al-Hilal fetched a collective £140m, commensurate to a year of Premier League TV money. Youth product Freddie Potts’ departure to Club Brugge for £10m disappointed some fans. Needs must if further players are to arrive. There is interest in Ireland’s World Cup playoff hero Troy Parrott, the striker at AZ Alkmaar, though attracting players to the Championship has its difficulties.

View image in fullscreen West Ham have cashed in on key players, such as Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham, to cushion their descent into the Championship. Photograph: Phil Walter/Getty Images

In the dugout remains Nuno Espírito Santo, who stayed when his departure had been expected. Nuno’s zen-like calm is required at a club where panic regularly sets in. The vacuum created by Sullivan’s situation, relegation and lack of transfer business heightens anxieties. A new season has arrived, with uninviting league fixtures against Burnley, Charlton, Watford and Wolves by 1 September. Karim Virani, previously a club employee who departed in 2020, more recently at Glasgow Rangers, has returned as interim chief executive. Attempts are being made to stitch West Ham into a semblance of unity.

This summer, the London Stadium played host to concerts from Take That and Metallica, and staged the Diamond League athletics meet in July, where Josh Kerr broke the world mile record. Thursday saw a bid confirmed to stage the 2029 World Athletics Championships, following an impasse between the club and the stadium owners. Further reminders that West Ham’s home will never be fully their own, 10 years after departing the Boleyn Ground.

Such were the terms Sullivan, Gold Sr and Brady agreed for a stadium that fans continue to resent, where Sullivan is unlikely to be made to feel welcome.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Vinícius Júnior and a fantasy world of transfers in the football lull
Sports.content:
THE CAPTIVE VOID OF NOBLE RAGE

“We were so close … At the end of the day, really, they made him an offer he couldn’t refuse … It shows where we’re trying to aim for the club … There has been a lot of stuff written in the papers that you have to take on the chin I’m afraid – they should be talking about how well the England cricket team are playing at the moment.” Words said not by Mikel Arteta about Arsenal missing out on Vinícius Júnior after the Brazilian megastar signed a new Real Madrid contract, but by Glenn Hoddle in 2002, as Tottenham missed out on signing … yes, Rivaldo. That last sentence was probably a dead giveaway. Tottenham’s solution to the Brazilian-shaped hole in their transfer ambitions was to sign Robbie Keane to his boyhood club. What might Arsenal do next? Eye up Cristian Romero, you say?

Arsenal’s unrequited chase for Vinícius brought to bear the fantasy world that fans reside in when the transfer window is open and no actual competitive football is being played. Just imagine what he might have done to defences in Our League. In that netherworld of reverie there are no wet Tuesday nights at Stoke, nobody gets knacked, nobody fails to settle, they just score a gazillion goals and outperform their xG. Imagine football heaven, it’s easy if you try.

There is a flip side. Transfer business, or lack thereof, can also lead to a summer of angst. See the social media disgrace wails of certain vocal fans at Liverpool and their exasperation that Virgil van Dijk, 73, is the sole senior Red Men centre-back. Perhaps the balm of signing Bradley Barcola will soothe, though that is not yet a DONE DEAL. Arsenal fans have already consoled themselves with the imminent addition of Bruno Guimarães; who needs Big Vin when the other Brazilian can supply passes to, er Gabriel Martinelli?

Each summer includes a deal that unlocks others. In a sign of the times, Madrid ponying up for a mega Vinícius deal rather than his doing one will likely shift tectonic plates. With him set to stay, Rodri whose winning of the 2024 Ballon d’Or caused an almighty strop from the Brazilian and his club, lest we forget, is now highly unlikely to head to the Bernabéu. With Kylian Mbappé already on silly money, and now Vinícius too, thus there is no room at the inn for the Spain captain. Instead, Manchester City’s main man and the Geopolitics World Cup’s very best player is said to want to join Barcelona, which would be a huge loss to his current club and Our League. Such is the transfer window, where it is far better to have loved and lost than never to have signed anyone at all.

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

It’s Friday night. It’s Littlewoods Cup time. Join Billy Munday for updates from Middlesbrough 0-0 Wrexham (1-0 on pens) from 8pm BST.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“We have been worried consistently and there has been one more step in [a] worrying direction every year, every part of the year. The trust is now gone for us, there is no way back for Infantino” – Norwegian Football Federation president Lise Klaveness calls on Gianni Infantino to do one, although the civil war engulfing Fifa has deepened with Mexico and Argentina backing him.

View image in fullscreen Lise Klaveness, having none of it. Photograph: Amanda Pedersen Giske/EPA

That might go some way to proving it. It would also help the rest of us help to show them the error of their ways” – Peter Holford (no, I’m not the ever-forgiving reader).

Sports.title: Manchester City reject Barcelona’s opening £38.5m bid for Rodri as talks continue
Sports.content:
Manchester City have rejected an offer of £38.5m (€45m) from Barcelona for Rodri and want at least £60m before allowing Spain’s World Cup-winning captain to depart.

Barcelona have emerged as Rodri’s preferred destination after talks with Real Madrid broke down this week. It is understood that the 30-year-old, who is now in the final year of his contract at City, has agreed personal terms with the Spanish champions after indicating that he would like to return to his homeland following the departure of Pep Guardiola.

Rodri moved to the Etihad in 2019 from Atlético Madrid and has turned down the offer of a lucrative extension. Yet City are believed to be adamant that he will not be allowed to leave for less than their asking price. Barcelona are continuing negotiations in the hope of reaching a compromise.

Rodri, who won the World Cup Golden Ball as the tournament’s best player last month, spoke to Barça’s manager, Hansi Flick, and sporting director, Deco, about a potential move on Wednesday.

The Spanish champions will be without Frenkie de Jong for several months after the Netherlands midfielder sustained a knee injury and have targeted Rodri as a replacement. He has had minor surgery on his back and will miss most of City’s pre-season programme.

City have signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m and remain in negotiations with Lille over a deal for Ayyoub Bouaddi. The Morocco midfielder could cost up to £80m but they could be tempted to bring in a more experienced replacement for Rodri should he depart, with Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández among those thought to be under consideration. The 25-year-old is also wanted by Real, whose manager, José Mourinho is said to not to have the news of being gazumped by their great rivals well. Reports in Spain have claimed that the 63-year-old is unhappy after making the signing of a central midfielder his priority on returning for a second stint at the Santiago Bernabéu.

Real have already brought in the winger Yan Diomande for £115m and Marc Cucurella, Bernardo Silva, Ibrahima Konaté, Denzel Dumfries and Carlos Espí, so they may have to balance the books by selling either Aurélien Tchouaméni and Eduardo Camavinga if they want to pursue Argentinian Fernández.

Crystal Palace have confirmed the signing of Takehiro Tomiyasu after a successful trial period. The former Arsenal defender has been training with Palace during pre-season and has done enough to earn an initial 12-month deal with the option of extending that by another two years. Tomiyasu becomes new manager Pierre Sage’s second signing of the summer after the arrival of Óscar Mingueza on a free transfer. Palace are expected to complete a deal for the USA youth international Zavier Gozo from Real Salt Lake in MLS.

Sports.title: Tottenham and Atlético in talks over Romero with Van de Ven set to sign new deal
Sports.content:
Tottenham are in talks with Atlético Madrid over the sale of Cristian Romero after categorically rejecting Arsenal’s approach for the Argentina defender and are expected to agree a new five-year deal with Micky van de Ven.

Romero has made no secret of his desire to leave Spurs despite signing a new four-year contract at the start of last season and had looked set to join Inter for a fee of around £35m. But Atlético are long-term suitors of the 28-year-old and are thought to be his preferred destination, with Diego Simeone’s side understood to be prepared to match Inter’s bid.

Reports in Spain on Friday suggested that personal terms have already been agreed with Romero, although his move may have to wait for Atlético to free up space in their squad before they can complete the transfer. Nahuel Molina, Romero’s Argentina teammate, is expected to join Roma while Aston Villa are hoping to sign Matteo Ruggeri.

Arsenal had also made their interest known as they search for a replacement for William Saliba, with the Frenchman out for an extended period due to a back issue. However, Tottenham – who have signed defenders Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi this summer – insisted that they did not want to sell to another Premier League club, least of all their north London rivals. Arsenal are also interested in Villa’s Ezri Konsa.

It is understood that Van de Ven had been considering his future in north London at the start of the summer after Tottenham narrowly avoided relegation last season. But the impact of the new manager, Roberto De Zerbi, has persuaded the Netherlands international to commit his future to the club after talks with his representatives.

Tottenham have already spent more than £200m on six new players this summer and are still in the market for a new attacker. Last week, De Zerbi said that they had “completed 60% of our project in the transfer market”.

Sports.title: Cristian Romero is one of the worst ever Premier League captain’s – he’s got serious anger issues
Sports.content:
Cristian Romero is one of the worst ever Premier League captain’s – he’s got serious anger issues

Cristian Romero has been labelled as one of the worst captains in Premier League history amid his impending Tottenham exit.

Those are the views of ex-Liverpool striker Dean Saunders and former Aston Villa forward Gabby Agbonlahor, who have slammed the Spurs star for his behaviour last season.

4 Romero was appointed as Spurs' captain last summer following Son Heung-min's departure Credit: Getty

Romero and Spurs finished in 17th place for the second straight top-flight campaign last term, which was his first as captain.

He played 23 games and received two red cards, also getting embroiled in a controversy at the end of the season.

The feisty centre-back flew to Argentina despite Tottenham having a must-win relegation clash on the final day.

Then, over the summer, he was involved in some World Cup chaos that saw his nation majorly criticised for their actions.

All of those factors led to Saunders calling him one of the worst skippers to have ever played in the Premier League.

He said on talkSPORT Breakfast: "Romero is up there with one of the worst captains in the history of the Premier League.

"Spurs have finished 17th and 17th, two years running. He was the captain so he can't be that good can he?

"And he's an absolute liability on the pitch. He's a walking red card and his behaviour in the World Cup after the whistle went sums him up."

Agbonlahor slams 'shocking' Romero

Agbonlahor agreed with Saunders' take on Romero when reacting to his comments on Drive on Friday afternoon.

"I think it's fair," the former England forward said, also criticising the Spurs defender. "As a captain, you have to be reliable.

4 Agbonlahor agreed with Saunders' claim that Romero is a 'liability' on the pitch Credit: Getty

"A captain is a role that's a privilege, you should be going around in the game and training ground setting standards.

"He's not the kind of captain you want...if you're struggling in a game you're not looking at him to lift you. He'd probably go and get sent off."

Agbonlahor added: "I think he's a liability...when he's at it, especially for Argentina, he's a top defender, but something about his ego says to be he thinks he's better than Spurs.

"I think he thinks Spurs are beneath him, the way he tried to stay in Argentina for the last game of the season, he probably got forced by his agent to get back.

"He's a liability, he's got anger issues, he should see someone about that because some of the tackles and red cards he got over his career have been shocking.

"I think in the Premier League now, you need to be able to trust all 22, 23 players not to give a silly red card away."

4 Romero has never been sent off for Argentina but has six reds for Spurs Credit: Getty

Agbonlahor continued to rip into Romero, questioning the 28-year-old's short fuse and differing attitude with club and country.

"Football has changed," he said. "It's different to 20 years ago when if someone's annoying you, you can leave one on them.

"You can't do it anymore, how many times has he done it? He's got frustrated by someone and left a bit on them and got sent off.

"You shouldn't do it anyway, but when you're captain and in your late 20s...

"He's good at tackling when it suits him - 40 caps for Argentina and zero red cards, but for Spurs six red cards, that says it all."

And now, Romero is set to leave Tottenham after five years...

4 The Spurs skipper is set to join Atletico after agreeing personal terms Credit: Getty

On the way out

Tottenham captain Romero has agreed personal terms to join Atletico Madrid, talkSPORT understands.

He held talks with Inter Milan this summer and was even linked to a shock move to north London rivals Arsenal.

But now, he looks set to be heading to Spain - and that's a move that Agbonlahor thinks suits him to a tee.

Diego Simeone's Atletico have become renowned for their aggressive approach on the pitch over the years....

"If there's a team that suit Romero, it's Atletico Madrid," he said.

"If there was a bet I could put on that he'd get the most red cards, it'd be on him."

Sports.title: Aston Villa could wait until end of window to make move for Premier League striker
Sports.content:
Aston Villa could wait until end of window to make move for Premier League striker

Aston Villa could delay trying to sign Nicolas Jackson until the end of the transfer window due to UEFA rules, talkSPORT understands.

The Villans have been heavily linked with a move for Jackson, who is free to leave Chelsea and is valued at around £65million.



4 Nicolas Jackson is currently away on Chelsea's pre-season tour of Australia and Asia Credit: Getty

Having spent the 2025/26 campaign away from Stamford Bridge on loan at Bayern Munich, the Senegal international now looks set for a clean break from the Blues.

Villa aren't the only club being tipped to make a play for Jackson, with Spurs also linked with the striker.

But with Unai Emery's side keen to strengthen after some high-profile departures - namely Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans - they could be interested in doing business with Chelsea again.



Knowing major sales would be required this summer to avoid falling foul of UEFA's financial restrictions, Villa sanctioned the departure of Rogers to the Blues for a British record £117million.

That wasn't the end of the two clubs' deals either, as Alejandro Garnacho then headed to Villa Park on loan.



talkSPORT previously reported that the Argentina international had been offered to Villa alongside Jackson in the wake of their deal to sign Rogers.

And while a move for the Chelsea striker remains a possibility, talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs has now revealed there are some obstacles that could delay any deal until later this summer.



Financial constraints

According to UEFA's transfer rules, multiple deals completed between the same clubs within a 45-day period is classified as a swap.

With Rogers heading to Stamford Bridge at the end of July, Villa and Chelsea still find themselves within this window.

This means that, if Villa were to sign Jackson now, they would have to reduce the profit made from the Rogers sale to the difference between that figure and how much was paid for Jackson.

4 Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea as their club-record signing Credit: Getty



4 Alejandro Garnacho linked up with the Villans on an initial loan deal shortly later Credit: Getty

Villa were able to avoid a similar situation with Garnacho by signing the winger on an initial loan deal with a conditional obligation to buy.

Speaking on talkSPORT's Transfer Insiders, reporter Ben Jacobs explained how the Midlands outfit could now bide their time over Jackson, in order to comply with UEFA rules.

Jacobs explained: “Villa do like Nicolas Jackson.

“We heard some reports that Tottenham were in - that's not my understanding. Spurs sources are denying that they're going to bid for Nicolas Jackson.



“And then if Villa are going to move, maybe the reason why there's no movement is; if both clubs are to reflect Morgan Rogers and should Jackson go to Villa, Nicolas Jackson [would go] positively on their books, because when you do these sales, you can take that transfer fee and you can put it on your annual books, and then if you've got an outlay, you can amortise it, which makes it a bit more palatable.

“But under the new UEFA rules, you can't do these mirrored or separate deals within a 45 day window."

4 Jackson has 30 goals in 81 games in a Chelsea shirt Credit: Getty

Jacobs explained: “If you roughly go back to when Morgan Rogers [moved to Chelsea], depending on when it was actually signed, and Chelsea might not have known that Villa were going to bid or potentially proceed with Jackson.



“But if you go back to that deal roughly, if it is to fall outside of a 45- day window, then it would likely suit both Villa and Chelsea to do that deal right at the end of the window, because we're definitely still within that 45-day period now."

Jacobs claimed UEFA restrictions have likely delayed any move by Villa for Jackson, while he also pointed to the striker's situation at Chelsea.

With new boss Xabi Alonso keen to take a look at the 25-year-old before sanctioning a sale, he has joined up with the Blues squad for their pre-season tour of Australia and Asia.

However, he still faces an uncertain future following the arrival of veteran striker Danny Welbeck from Brighton.



Jacobs continued: “Maybe that's why we haven't had any update on Nicholas Jackson's future, coupled with the fact that Xabi Alonso has just needed to see particularly both [Liam] Delap and Jackson in preseason before maybe inputting which one of them, or potentially both, he wants to depart.”

Sports.title: Trailblazing Premier League official Sian Massey-Ellis retires and instantly lands new job
Sports.content:
Premier League assistant referee Sian Massey-Ellis has announced her immediate retirement from officiating.

The trailblazing sideline official will now begin work as the Football Association's (FA) Senior Manager of Women Referees.

3 Massey-Ellis never wilted in the face of criticism from players Credit: Getty

Massey-Ellis' new role centres on supporting and developing the ever-growing pool of female officials in addition to inspiring the next generation.

Massey-Ellis: 'Greatest honour to serve the game'

“From standing beneath the Premier League sign before my very first match to officiating at FIFA World Cups, UEFA European Championships, Champions League finals and across domestic fixtures and competitions in England, football has taken me on a journey beyond anything I could ever have imagined," Massey-Ellis said in a statement.

"Every opportunity has been a privilege and one I have never taken for granted.

“Throughout my career, football has challenged me, tested my resilience and pushed me to become a better professional and person.

"While there have been unforgettable highs and difficult moments, what I will treasure most are the people and experiences that have defined my journey.

"I am incredibly grateful to Pro Ref, The FA, FIFA and UEFA for the opportunities they gave me, as well as every coach, mentor, colleague and match official I have had the privilege of working alongside.

"Above all, I owe an enormous debt of thanks to my family, whose unwavering support, sacrifices and belief made every achievement possible.

“Although I am stepping away from the touchline, I am not stepping away from football.

"If my journey has helped change perceptions, open doors or inspire even one young person to believe they belong in the game, then I will consider that one of my greatest achievements.

"I'm excited by the opportunity to help support, develop and inspire the next generation of match officials, giving something back to a sport that has done so much for me.

3 The 40-year-old begins her new role in September Credit: Getty

“As I prepare for one final walk onto the pitch, I leave with nothing but gratitude. It has been the greatest honour to serve the game I love and represent English officiating.

"To the young girl who simply loved refereeing and dreamed of reaching the very top - we did it.

"Thank you, football."

Pro Ref Chief Refereeing Officer Howard Webb added Massey-Ellis 'has been nothing short of a powerhouse' over the course of her officiating career.

"She has done us proud time and time again - domestically and on the international stage, breaking multiple barriers and setting the standard for those coming through in her footsteps," Webb added.

History-making

Massey-Ellis hangs up the flag having become just the second female to be an assistant referee in Premier League history, with Wendy Toms the first to do so.

3 Massey-Ellis has paved the way for the next generation of female officials Credit: Getty

She went on to be the first female involved in the men's FA Cup final and the Community Shield.

Massey-Ellis was also a trailblazer internationally, becoming the first female selected to officiate a men's European match when she was an assistant referee for a Europa League fixture in 2019.

She also represented England at four UEFA Women's Euro tournaments as well as the 2019 and 2023 FIFA Women's World Cups.

The 40-year-old's vast achievements on the sideline earned her an MBE in 2017 for her services to football.

Sports.title: World Cup winner showcases incredible physique aged 56 and gives fans achievable workout tip
Sports.content:
France legend Bixente Lizarazu has done it all in his career and now he's handing out top workout tips to his fans on social media.

The ex-Bayern Munich star, now 56, won it all as a player.

2 Lizarazu lifts the World Cup in 1998 Credit: Getty Images - Getty



He scooped the Champions League, European Championship, World Cup and six Bundesliga titles, plus the Intercontinental Cup and individual awards from UEFA and FIFA.

And the left-back did it in the era of Roberto Carlos too.

Since retiring in 2006, Lizarazu hasn't taken his foot off the gas, rather he's put his foot to the floor.

Had his Weet-a-Bix

By 2009 he was a European Champion, this time in the sport of Brazilian jiu jitsu.

He won it in the Blue Belt Senior 1 Light Division.

His physical ability has always been of repute with Zinedine Zidane once claiming only Lizarazu could have stopped him getting sent off in the 2006 World Cup final.



Not only did the 97-cap France legend take to BJJ, he has also been surfing, skiing, diving and cycling in his retirement.

And now he's showcased his outrageous physique once more, this time warning his fans to look after their bodies.



He posted a workout video on Instagram where he only used his bodyweight or small weights.

With it, Lizarazu insisted that with age it's important to stop your body losing muscle, but that doesn't mean you have to lift heavy.



He said in the caption: "Weight training is important after 40, essential after 50… after that, I don't know, we'll see!

"My goal isn't to gain muscle, but to avoid losing it.

"Are you familiar with sarcopenia?

"It's the progressive loss of muscle mass and strength, mainly due to aging. We all go through it, sooner or later…

"So it's good to have a complete, personalized weight training protocol.

"I have several.

2 Lizarazu is one of the best left-backs in football history Credit: getty images



"You'll notice that I only use small equipment (dumbbells, kettlebells, TRX, bodyweight)."

A host of former players hailed him in the comments with ex-Liverpool and France star Djibril Cisse saying simply: "Incredible."

Ex-Lyon and Nice star Anthony Mounier added: "Transfer window time!! If any club is looking for a left-back, I know one who's still available."

And former France goalkeeper Gregory Coupet said: "Beautiful animal."

Sports.title: When is the Carabao Cup second round draw? Date, start time and how to follow as Chelsea and Tottenham enter competition
Sports.content:
When is the Carabao Cup second round draw? Date, start time and how to follow as Chelsea and Tottenham enter competition

The Carabao Cup has now kicked off the new English football season and the second round draw is coming up fast.

An action-packed weekend of cup football is well underway and as teams progress, focus will shift to the draw.

3 The journey to lifting the Carabao Cup trophy is officially underway Credit: Getty

For successful clubs in Round One, they could well be handed a huge tie in the second round too, as some giants join.

Both Chelsea and Tottenham are going to be in the Round Two draw, having not qualified for Europe last season.

There are also another nine Premier League sides getting involved, potentially being put at risk of a major upset.

Here's all you need to know about the Carabao Cup draw...

When is the Carabao Cup second round draw?

The draw for Round Two of the Carabao Cup will take place on Monday, August 10 at approximately 7:20pm.

It will be held before Plymouth Argyle face local rivals Exeter City in what is the final game of the first round.

Second round ties will be played on the week commencing August 24.

How to follow the Carabao Cup draw

The second round draw will be broadcast live on Sky Sports Football in the build-up to the Devon derby.

It will be part of their match coverage from Home Park.

talkSPORT and talkSPORT.com will also be right across the latest.

3 Xabi Alonso is set to find out his first Carabao Cup opponent as Chelsea boss Credit: Getty

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

Which Premier League clubs are joining?

There are 11 Premier League clubs joining the Carabao Cup at the second round, with nine others not yet involved.

Chelsea and Spurs are among the 11 sides without European football, with Newcastle and Nottingham Forest in the same boat.

3 Tottenham are entering the competition at the second round after a poor last season Credit: AFP

Leeds also won't be playing in Europe, along with Everton, Brentford, Fulham, and newly-promoted Coventry, Ipswich and Hull.

Arsenal, Manchester City, Liverpool and Manchester United are four of the nine clubs joining the Carabao Cup in the third round.

How does the second round draw work?

The Carabao Cup second round follows the same format as the first round, splitting the competition into regions.

Teams are split into Northern and Southern sections.

So, they will be drawn against a club that are in their region.

This will then change for the third round, when all teams can be drawn against each other no matter their location.

Sports.title: Gary Neville warned ‘promotion lunatic’ could stop Salford City’s League Two title hopes
Sports.content:
Peterborough United chairman Darragh MacAnthony believes 'promotion lunatic' Steve Evans could derail Salford City's title hopes.

Salford's 2026/27 campaign marks the start of a new era having undergone a major rebrand.



3 Salford have been in League Two since 2019 Credit: Getty

The Ammies, who have languished in League Two since earning promotion from National League in 2019, have changed their badge to a round one and returned to orange as their predominant colour as opposed to red.

There's also a new face in the dugout at Moor Lane, with Peter Cklamovski taking over from Karl Robinson after the latter was axed following last season's League Two play-off final defeat against Notts County.

Salford's ownership group, which includes Gary Neville and David Beckham, will hope Cklamovski can take what he learned as a previous understudy of Ange Postecoglou and steer the club to the third tier.



Cklamovski, who was previously the head coach of the Malaysia national team, has also been backed in the transfer market, with eight new faces arriving.

One of the new players through the door is striker Macaulay Langstaff, who joined from Championship side Millwall.



Langstaff has already proven himself capable in the fourth tier, scoring 28 goals in 46 fixtures for Notts County during the 2023/24 campaign.

MacAnthony: 'Never write off' Evans

Despite Salford's mass changes this summer, MacAnthony warned Evans, who is in charge of Bristol Rovers, could easily upset the apple cart.



When asked who he believed on talkSPORT's White and Jordan will win League Two, MacAnthony said: "You'd have to say Salford, with the amount of business they've done.

"But never write off Steve Evans, I always say that.

"The guy's a serial winner, he's a promotion lunatic. He's won more promotions than I've had Guinness.

3 The Salford role is Cklamovski's first in European football Credit: Getty

"There's a few biggies that you couldn't write off, but I would say Salford for what they've spent this summer, and I'm well aware of what they've spent, you'd expect them to win the league."



How has Evans performed at Bristol Rovers?

Evans initially took over the Gas last December on a deal until the end of the season.

At the time, the club was in the relegation zone of League Two.

But Evans dragged the club to safety and even oversaw a sensational run of 11 wins from their last 14 league fixtures, helping the Gas finish 14th.

Evans has since signed a two-year deal to stay on as Rovers' manager.

The 63-year-old will be targeting his first promotion since the 2022/23 campaign, when he led Stevenage to a second-place finish in League Two.

3 Bristol Rovers are the ninth club Evans has managed Credit: Getty



It was the eighth promotion across English football Evans had overseen throughout his managerial career.

Yet a ninth with Rovers may prove to be the most special of the lot.

Sports.title: EFL club’s chairman responds to Adrian Durham’s shock relegation claim
Sports.content:
Peterborough United chairman Darragh MacAnthony has called for calm in the transfer market amid Adrian Durham's relegation fears.

Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, Posh fan Durham voiced his concerns that the club's lack of activity in the summer window has the club at serious risk of the drop.

3 Posh are aiming for a return to the second tier after four seasons away Credit: Getty

"We lost three of our best players this summer, they've not been replaced," Durham said.

"We haven't signed a player for a month.

"The manager, Luke Williams, says Posh are targeting promotion. With the squad we've got right now, Posh will be relegated.

"If they don't add at least four players to go straight in the first team, a right-back, a winger, a No.10 and a six, Peterborough will be in massive trouble."

Patience is a virtue

However, MacAnthony, who has been the club's chairman since 2006, was quick to allay Durham's fears and claimed Posh are quietly working from a transfer shortlist that has been in place since May.

"I can basically give up what we're trying to do and I can go sign plan C, D and E, and they're not the players we wanted," MacAnthony said on talkSPORT's White and Jordan.

"Or, I can just hang in there and play this the way I'm playing it, which I think will be the right thing for our football club.

"We do need four or five signings, potentially five."

One position MacAnthony didn't believe needed upgrading was the right-back spot.

At present, 21-year-old James Dornelly and Carl Johnston are the main options to play on the right side of defence, with MacAnthony describing the duo as 'two very good right-backs and everyone knows that.'

3 MacAnthony is comfortable with Posh waiting for the right player rather than stressing in the transfer market Credit: talkSPORT

"We have a good young squad, we have a great manager," MacAnthony continued.

"They've been working their backsides off all summer and I just hate the fact they're getting hammered.

"The manager, his staff, the work they've put in with the players... And it's not just Adrian, it's everyone else saying, 'They're going to be bottom, they're going to be relegated.'

"My god, cut us some slack."

MacAnthony: 'Everyone forgets' we've made play-offs in three of last five seasons

It must be noted Durham did back MacAnthony to bring in the right players as Posh look to avoid a similar slump in League One.

Accelerated by injuries to three of the club's best players, Peterborough won just one of their last 15 league fixtures.

3 Williams has won 14 of his first 37 games in charge of the club Credit: Getty

The alarming run of form meant Posh ended the season in 18th and four points clear of the relegation zone.

Yet MacAnthony was quick to point out that type of season is an exception rather than the norm in recent years and reiterated a message of patience in the transfer market.

"I know we finished really badly, but it's not where Peterborough wants to be," MacAnthony said.

"Three of the last five years, we've been in the play-offs, but everyone forgets that.

"I know what we need, the manager knows what we need. But we want the ones we want. What we don't want is worse options."

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal star joins Premier League rival on free transfer after successful trial
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace have completed the signing of ex-Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu on a free transfer.

The Japan international joins the Eagles after a successful trial, having been without a club since his departure from Ajax at the end of the 2025/26 campaign.

5 Tomiyasu is looking for a new club after spending the first part of his summer at the World Cup with Japan Credit: Getty

An Eagle has landed

After training with Palace in recent weeks, Tomiyasu has now been officially confirmed as the club's second summer signing.

His arrival follows Spanish defender Oscar Mingueza, who also moved to Selhurst Park on a free transfer following his exit from LaLiga outfit Celta Vigo.

Tomiyasu joined up with with Palace last week for their pre-season training in Como, Italy.

He later featured in their friendly win over Al Ula on Friday, with his performance paving a way for a return to the Premier League.

Reacting to his move back to English football, Tomiyasu told Palace: “I’m excited to get started.

"This club is in a good moment, winning three titles in two seasons. Here is where I wanted to be.”

Comeback trail

Tomiyasu's arrival in south London brings an end to his period as a free agent after leaving Ajax at the end of last season.

He joined the Dutch giants in December after mutually agreeing to end his contract with Arsenal last summer.

The Japan star signed for the club whilst still recovering from a long-term knee injury that had kept him out of action for almost a year prior.

But having only penned a six-month deal until the end of the season, Tomiyasu ultimately departed having made just nine appearances.

5 Tomiyasu was a fan favourite at Arsenal, despite being heavily affected by injury Credit: Getty

5 Pierre Sage is looking to make his mark at Conference League winners Crystal Palace Credit: Getty

He went on to feature three times for Japan in their run to the last-32 of the 2026 World Cup.

With a number of Palace's first-team stars yet to report back for training after the World Cup, they Tomiyasu was allowed to join the team to train and work on his fitness ahead of the new season.

And it appears he took full advantage of the opportunity, with Tomiyaus now set to bring vital Premier League experience to Selhurst Park.

Crystal Palace are currently gearing up for their first season under new boss Pierre Sage, who was named as Oliver Glasner's successor in June.

They had been in the market for a new defender as key man Maxence Lacroix leaving to join Chelsea in a deal worth £52m.

talkSPORT previously reported that Palace were considering Augsburg’s Chrislain Matsima as a potential replacement, while Tomiyasu himself is capable of playing at centre-back.

5 Tomiyasu featured in just one game in his final season at Arsenal due to a knee injury Credit: Getty

Fresh start

Tomiyasu is looking to get his career back on track after seeing his last few seasons blighted by injury.

He departed Arsenal in July 2025 following the mutual decision to terminate his contract a year early, and had not featured for the club since the previous October.

The Japan star had missed the start of the 2024/25 season due to a previous knee injury that needed surgery in 2023.

But another knee issue saw him go under the knife again in January 2025, ultimately leading to his early departure from north London.

Tomiyasu joined Arsenal from Serie A side Bologna in a deal rising to £20million in 2021, and featured 84 times overall, scoring two goals and providing two assists.

After joining Ajax in December last year, he made his debut in January, but only eight further appearances followed.

5 Tomiyasu hadn't started a league game for any club in almost two seasons before his full Ajax debut in March Credit: Getty

The ex-Premier League star ultimately played only 236 minutes of football, failing to earn a new contract as the Amsterdam outfit finished a disappointing fifth in the Eredivisie.

Following his departure, Tomiyasu penned an emotional statement, where he shared his sadness at not having played a bigger role.

He wrote on Instagram: “It was only five months but I would like to thank all who support Ajax.

“Obviously it was not the season we wanted and no one is satisfied with how it ended.

“Personally, I joined this club in January after such a long rehab, I wanted to give much more, I should have done much more for this club but it didn’t work out well."

Sports.title: Freddie Flintoff leaves England Lions coaching job: Cricket legend announces departure after two-year stint - with role 'saving' him after life-changing Top Gear crash
Sports.content:
Andrew Flintoff has stepped down as head coach of England Lions after nearly two years to focus on his new role at Australia’s Sydney Thunder franchise in the Big Bash League.

Flintoff, who also plans to spend more time on his TV career and with his family, was not in the running to replace Brendon McCullum as England’s Test coach, and faced a potential clash between his Thunder and Lions work.

The 47-year-old, one of England's greatest and most popular cricketers of all-time, took charge of his country's second string team in September 2024 and previously credited the role with 'saving' him after his near-fatal Top Gear crash.

Flintoff was hailed for creating an impressive environment and helping to develop several talented young players, yet he is leaving the job with immediate effect.

He said: 'Unfortunately I’ve made the decision to step away from my role with the Lions.

'Not only have I enjoyed my time having the opportunity to work with the best young cricketers in the country, but have taken great pride in seeing them develop.

Andrew 'Freddie' Flintoff has stepped away from his role as England Lions head coach

Flintoff (pictured with former Test head coach Brendon McCullum) was praised for his work

'I’d like to thank the coaches and staff for all their passion, tireless work and support they give everyday.

'In particular, Ed Barney who I’ve loved working with and was so lucky to have as a performance director, and obviously Rob (Key) for trusting me with one of the most important roles in English cricket.

'I can’t wait to get started with the Thunder later in the year and see where coaching takes me.'

Flintoff's time with the Lions was the latest step on his coaching journey following his return to the game after his life-changing crash while filming Top Gear in December 2022.

Flintoff was airlifted to hospital after the incident having suffered serious facial and rib injuries before he faced a lengthy period recovering, where he initially refused to leave his house except for medical appointments.

Flintoff previously had little involvement in cricket following his retirement in 2010, focusing instead on a hugely successful TV career.

He joined the England Lions having also coached Northern Superchargers in The Hundred. Flintoff similarly spent time around England's senior team.

Speaking in 2025 on a Disney+ documentary about his career and recovery from the car crash, Flintoff opened up on how important his return to the sport had been.

'This sounds awful: part of me thinks I should have been killed,' he said. 'Part of me thinks I wish I had died. I didn’t want to kill myself, I won’t mistake the two things.

'I wasn’t wishing, I was thinking: that would have been so much easier. Now I try to take the attitude, you know what, the sun will come up tomorrow, and my kids will still give me a hug. I feel in a better place now.

'If one thing’s come out of it which is positive it’s being back in cricket. It’s probably the one thing that saved me.

'I’ve been welcomed back into that fold. It’s such a good place. I feel it’s safe. I have moments when I’m sat in a dressing room and I’m watching a game of cricket surrounded by cricketers and friends, and I’m able to forget.'

Flintoff (pictured in 2018) was involved in a near-fatal car crash while filming Top Gear

In the press release announcing his exit from the Lions, the ECB's performance director Ed Barney added: 'Fred has helped to transform the Lions environment into a programme that has had a major impact on young players.

'By creating an environment that both supports and pushes excellence at all times he has helped bring forward a new generation of young players.

'Coaches have also flourished alongside him, whether early in their coaching journey or with decades of experience, and he has consistently maximised the expertise around the group.

'We wish him the best in the next stage of his coaching career and look forward to a time he returns to the English game.'

The former England and Sussex all-rounder Mike Yardy will step in to take charge of next week’s four-day match at Beckenham between Pakistan and a Professional County Club Select XI.

Sports.title: Former Man United star Nicky Butt reveals he is BANNED from his local tip after blazing row with staff
Sports.content:
Former Man United star Nicky Butt reveals he is BANNED from his local tip after blazing row with staff

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former Manchester United midfielder Nicky Butt has revealed he is banned from his local tip following a bizarre row with a member of staff.

Butt, 51, says he got into a blazing confrontation with a worker at the tip who prevented him from entering because he thought his Range Rover was a commercial vehicle as the seats were down.

The former England star claims the attendant then chased him after he defied his orders and drove into the site, thought to be the Woodhouse Lane Recycling Centre in Altrincham.

Butt said on The Good, The Bad and The Football Podcast that the incident had left him 'raging'.

'I've got a lot of c**p from the house, bit of cardboard . . . I missed the bin man last week, so I've got a few smelly bags,' he said.

'So I put the windows down, obviously my seats were down and apparently I'm not going in because of it.

Nicky Butt has revealed he got into a bizarre row with an attendant at his local tip

'He said to me, "Your windows are blacked out because you're sneaking stuff into it, into the tip." And I went, 'No, it's standard, mate''.

Butt added: 'I thought, well, I'm there now, I'm gonna go for it. So I've got up the ramp, I see this bloke getting up . . . trying to chase me up the hill, but he's got his walkie-talkie out.

'So I've literally got up the top, throw all the bags out, and I'm going back down the hill, and he's going mad at me. Anyway, I'm banned from the tip.'

Butt appears on the podcast with former Man United team-mate Paul Scholes, and comedian and television presenter Paddy McGuinness.

The ex-United stars have caused controversy on the show after being criticised for their opinions on Lisandro Martinez.

Butt won the Champions League, six Premier League titles and three FA Cups at Old Trafford. He left in the summer of 2004 to join Newcastle in a deal worth £2.5million.

Since his retirement, Butt has been chief executive of League Two side Salford City and also served as head of Man United's academy for five years.

Sports.title: Newcastle did NOT want to sell £75m Bruno Guimaraes - but 'very emotional' captain asked to leave for Arsenal, reveals transfer chief
Sports.content:
Newcastle sporting director Ross Wilson says the club 'didn't want to sell' captain Bruno Guimaraes.

The 28-year-old midfielder is set to leave the Magpies and join Arsenal for a fee of £75million, although confirmation of the move has not been officially announced yet.

Guimaraes' seemingly impending departure comes following a tough summer for Newcastle, who have already seen Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali exit during the transfer window while head coach Eddie Howe resigned last week, with Matthias Jaissle officially appointed as his replacement on Wednesday.

Speaking to reporters at Newcastle's pre-season training camp in Spain, Wilson said: 'We didn't want to sell Bruno. It wasn't in the plan to sell Bruno. None of us — or ownership — wanted to sell Bruno.

'He's our captain, he was very, very important to us and the debate over his price — it's a world-record fee for a player of his age.

'What we had to weigh up was, very respectfully from Bruno with his behaviour towards us, very emotionally as well, effectively told us he wanted to leave and move on.

Newcastle sporting director Ross Wilson has said the club 'didn't want to sell' captain Bruno Guimaraes (pictured)

'That doesn't mean he can go but it certainly plays a part in what our thinking is when we hit a certain range of number. But there's no point in saying it was part of our strategy and was in our thinking this summer — it wasn't.

'But we have got to be flexible and react to things that happen. It might have been in our plan to sign one player but we didn't get him so we move on to another. We can only be honest about that.'

Sports.title: Revealed: Defiant David Sullivan believes he is being 'bullied' into staying away from West Ham stadium as owner, 77 - who is accused of sexual misconduct - prepares to face crowd after explosive Panorama allegations
Sports.content:
David Sullivan plans to defy advice to stay away from West Ham’s first home game of the season because the club’s co-owner, accused of multiple counts of sexual misconduct, feels he is being ‘bullied’ into missing it, Daily Mail Sport understands.

The 77-year-old, the club’s largest shareholder, resigned as co-chair in June ahead of the airing of a BBC Panorama and Times investigation in which seven women accused Sullivan of predatory behaviour, which he strongly denies.

The operators of the London Stadium recommended to West Ham that Sullivan not attend the match against Portsmouth in the Carabao Cup on Saturday over fears of potential fan unrest while the club’s fan advisory board said his presence would cause ‘offence and upset’.

That feeling is shared by insiders who believed the 77-year-old’s resignation would signal a fresh start for the club, with many staggered that Sullivan plans to be there. One staff member told Daily Mail Sport they had planned to attend the Portsmouth game but would now stay away due to the ‘circus’ and added that the club ‘cannot be serious about wanting to do well if this is what is planned for the season ahead.’

Sullivan is understood not to have made a final decision but sources close to the co-owner told Daily Mail Sport that he’s worried about the state of the team and lack of transfer activity heading into their first season in the Championship in 14 years and feels he needs to watch the game live. They also said Sullivan feels he’s being ‘bullied' by 'keyboard warriors’ into staying away.

Sullivan was accused in June of preying on a string of women, some in their teens, during his time as a newspaper chief stretching back to the 1980s as seven women came forward to give detailed accounts of predatory behaviour they had experienced, including pressuring them for sex or oral sex by suggesting it would help their careers. Sullivan described the allegations as ‘factually incorrect and entirely false’.

David Sullivan believes he is being 'bullied' into staying away from West Ham amid allegations of sexual misconduct

Sources close to Sullivan also claimed he’s received numerous messages from fans urging him to attend despite his presence at matches last season sparking continued protests from spectators against his ownership, including marches, boycotts, sit-ins, black balloons and thousands of fans brandishing red cards.

The Panorama investigation revealed that Sullivan had been banned from contact with West Ham women’s and youth teams for the past three years.

London Stadium’s operator has asked to be made aware of any planned Sullivan visits so it can implement its own safety measures. West Ham are said to have told the operator that it does not consider there to be an ongoing safeguarding risk associated with Sullivan attending the stadium.

Until recently, it appeared as though Sullivan’s grip on West Ham was loosening when it was announced in June that Vanessa Gold, daughter of former co-owner David, had agreed to sell part of their stake in the club to fellow shareholder Daniel Kretinsky. The move that would have seen the Czech billionaire overtake Sullivan as leading shareholder.

Last week, however, a new announcement confirmed that Gold had accepted a new offer from a consortium led by former Newcastle co-owner Amanda Staveley for her shares. Staveley agreed to buy a 25.1 per cent stake for £150million, which values the club at around £600million, and would still leave Sullivan as the leading stakeholder.

Staveley, though, has reportedly also made an offer to Sullivan, who is believed to be open to selling his stake in the club but values it at much more.

Sports.title: Inside Jake Paul's plot to overthrow the UFC: How influencer plans to get the upper hand on Dana White... and extend an olive branch to Ronda Rousey
Sports.content:
Inside Jake Paul's plot to overthrow the UFC: How influencer plans to get the upper hand on Dana White... and extend an olive branch to Ronda Rousey

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jake Paul has never been shy about declaring war on the establishment.

He has spent years accusing Dana White of underpaying fighters, publicly challenged the UFC president on everything from athlete welfare to revenue sharing and repeatedly insisted there is room for a genuine rival in mixed martial arts.

Now, he believes he finally has one.

This week, Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) completed a landmark merger with the Professional Fighters League (PFL), creating a combat sports company that combines boxing, MMA and entertainment under one banner.

The PFL name will gradually disappear over the coming months before being retired completely in January 2027, when the organization officially becomes MVP MMA. The combined company boasts almost 400 athletes worldwide, blending PFL's roster with MVP's rapidly growing boxing stable.

It is the biggest structural shake-up in MMA since the UFC cemented its dominance more than a decade ago.

Jake Paul (pictured above) has never been shy about declaring war on the establishment

He has spent years accusing Dana White of underpaying fighters, publicly challenged the UFC president on everything from athlete welfare to revenue sharing

Nobody inside MVP is pretending Dana White's empire is about to crumble overnight. But behind the scenes, the ambition is crystal clear.

'We know we're not going to overtake the UFC in the near future,' MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian said. 'This is a long term plan and over time we can close in on their position and create a Nike-versus-Adidas dynamic, or a Pepsi-versus-Coke dynamic, over the next seven to 10 years.

'We started this company five years ago and have been pioneers in boxing and in changing the way people consume content. We delivered the first live professional sporting event on Netflix.

'When we decided to enter MMA, we always said that if it proved successful, we would do more. Now, we the advantage of world-class infrastructure, elite fighters and the leadership of John Martin as CEO of the overall platform. We are not here to mess around.'

The merger instantly transforms MVP from a boxing promoter into a genuine multi-sport combat sports company.

Former PFL chief executive John Martin now oversees the wider business as CEO, while Jake Paul and Bidarian remain on the board, with Bidarian continuing to lead MVP Boxing alongside the promotion's blockbuster events.

Yet while the structure has changed, the philosophy has not.

From day one, Jake Paul has built his business around one message: fighters deserve more money. That message now sits at the heart of MVP's long-term strategy.

Daily Mail Sport sat down with Nakisa Bidarian to talk about how he and Paul are looking to reshape the economics of MMA

'The focus has always been to give at least 50 per cent of revenue back to the athletes,' Bidarian explained. 'If you look at traditional stick-and-ball sports that operate with those kinds of revenue-sharing models, they've created enormous enterprise value.

'When athletes receive a fair share, they're more invested, more committed, the product improves, and there's greater alignment across the sport.'

The comments represent another direct challenge to the UFC's long-standing business model, where fighter pay has remained one of the sport's most fiercely debated issues.

But simply paying athletes more is only one part of the plan. MVP believes it can also create stars in a way its rivals cannot.

'It's about branding, storytelling, exposure, engagement and producing content 24/7,' Bidarian said. 'It's about presenting our athletes for what they are - some of the best fighters in the world.

'Nobody does that better than MVP and Jake Paul. Our first MVP MMA event was a tremendous success and this merger turbocharges our ability to build on that momentum.'

The next battle will be fought in free agency.

MVP knows it cannot approach contracted UFC fighters, but once those deals expire, the landscape changes.

Bidarian believes PFL star Dakota Ditcheva has what it takes to become a global super star

'In MMA, just like in boxing, if a fighter is under contract you can't interfere with that,' Bidarian said. 'You have to wait until they become free agents.

'For example, the 155-pound champion Usman, who fought on Friday night, has just completed the final fight of his contract. I'm sure the UFC will try to re-sign him.

'But whenever a fighter comes out of contract with the UFC, of course we'll take a look. If they're the right fit for us, and we're the right fit for them, we'd love to make that partnership happen.'

The ambition stretches well beyond signing one or two marquee names.

'Our goal is to become the Pepsi to their Coke, the Adidas to their Nike, and eventually make this a genuine two-horse race,' Bidarian said. 'Sometimes we'll be ahead, sometimes they'll be ahead.

'But make no mistake, there's a real opportunity for a fighter-first platform. Very quickly, we're going to establish ourselves as the leading alternative.

'And in seven to 10 years' time, MVP will be the culturally relevant, empowerment-driven brand that Gen Z, Gen Alpha and even Gen Beta are focused on.'

One major advantage MVP believes it holds is flexibility.

Former UFC heavyweight champion Francis Ngannou remains central to the company's plans

Unlike publicly listed companies, Bidarian insists remaining privately owned allows the organization to pursue aggressive deals without shareholders dictating every financial decision.

'We intend to remain a private company for the foreseeable future because it provides us with a level of financial flexibility that public companies simply cannot match,' he said.

'In many ways, I would love for the UFC to announce tomorrow that they were increasing fighter pay to 50 per cent of revenue. But they can't. Doing so would significantly impact their margins, lower their enterprise value and ultimately affect the wealth of their owners.

'We have the freedom to be more aggressive in how we structure agreements and attract the best talent in the world.'

The roster itself is expected to evolve rapidly. Former UFC heavyweight champion Francis Ngannou remains central to the company's plans.

'That's absolutely what we want,' Bidarian said. 'Francis and I have spoken several times. He's excited to get back competing. He already has a relationship with the PFL, so it's just a case of making sure everyone is aligned on how we move forward. But yes, absolutely, Francis Ngannou is going to be part of what we're building.'

Women's MMA will also become a cornerstone of the new promotion.

Bidarian revealed he has already spoken to former UFC superstar Ronda Rousey about the future of the sport.

MVP already enjoys a close relationship with Matchroom through their recent boxing alliance, and Bidarian believes the partnership could eventually stretch beyond the squared circle

'Ronda Rousey is the most dominant female combat sports star in history in terms of popularity,' he said. 'She'd be more than welcome to be involved in MVP MMA in whatever role she wants. I spoke to her yesterday and listened to her thoughts on what we need to do.'

He also believes the promotion already possesses its next crossover superstar.

'Women's MMA will be a major focus for us. We have Dakota Ditcheva, who I believe is the most marketable female MMA fighter in the world.

'She's still young, undefeated, an outstanding striker and has enormous potential. We're excited to build around that.'

There may even be opportunities for crossover with boxing.

MVP already enjoys a close relationship with Matchroom through their recent boxing alliance, and Bidarian believes the partnership could eventually stretch beyond the squared circle and into their 'talent agency'.

'Listen, if Matchroom's talent from their talent agency become free agents, of course we'll have those discussions. We have a great working relationship with Eddie and Matchroom.

'The two MMA athletes they announced - Tom Aspinall and Ian Machado Garry - are both under UFC contracts, so there are no discussions to be had there for the moment but should they become available that's different.

Bidarian revealed he has already spoken to former UFC superstar Ronda Rousey (winning her contest with Gina Carano above) about the future of the sport

'I do think there's a huge long-term opportunity for Matchroom and MVP as combined entities. That's not today, and probably not three years from now. But when you think about Eddie's position in men's boxing, what we've built in women's boxing, and what we're going to build in MMA, I think there's a very clear path to what's possible over the next five to 10 years.'

For now, the UFC remains comfortably on top.

Dana White has already dismissed the merger between MVP and PFL, joking that it combines 'two organizations that struggle to sell tickets', while TKO president Mark Shapiro has taken a more measured stance, welcoming legitimate competition.

But inside MVP, nobody is looking for a quick knockout.

Instead, Jake Paul and Nakisa Bidarian are preparing for a long fight – one they believe could eventually reshape the economics of MMA.

They are not promising to replace the UFC.

They are trying to become something the sport has never truly had before: a genuine alternative.

Sports.title: Some of the elites criticising Gianni Infantino are sheer hypocrites. How can the money-obsessed leeches behind the Super League expect us to listen to their confected moral outrage as they bleed our beloved game dry, writes IAN HERBERT
Sports.content:
The most preposterous man in football is staggering on, drowning in such vanity and ego that he cannot see how he embarrasses himself, so perhaps that’s why the biggest hypocrites of another dark week for football appear to have got away with it.

On Sunday, Real Madrid decided to weigh in on the Gianni Infantino scandal, instructing their media people to put out a sanctimonious statement welcoming the scrapping of the egghead’s plans to sell off a slice of the World Cup, and thanking UEFA for fulfilling their ‘duty’ to ‘protect football’.

You really could not make some of this stuff up. Yes, that moralising really did come from the same Real Madrid whose avarice stank football out when they led the contemptible group of 12 clubs who attempted the European Super League breakaway coup, a few years back.

Infantino’s intellectual and moral decrepitude may have been there for us all to see in his email offering nations a small cash consideration if they back his plans to raise $20billion, but have we forgotten the European club men with whiteboards and coloured marker pens, explaining their own despicable little earner in 2021?
