World.title: US dollar exchange rate continues to rise in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,523.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,520.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,530 Iraqi dinars and 1,520 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,525.5 and 1,525 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq to increase production from Kirkuk oil fields
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair announced on Thursday plans to increase oil production from the Kirkuk oilfields.

The decision intends to capitalize on a recent agreement with Turkey for exporting oil to the port of Ceyhan.

This move also aims to circumvent the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and increase Iraq’s oil exports via ports on the Mediterranean.

The instruction utilizes the recently expanded Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline deal, with the goal of increasing exports from 180,000 barrels per day to approximately 750,000 barrels per day.

Khudair stated that increasing production lays the groundwork for boosting export volumes through Turkey to 1.5 million barrels per day.

Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO) has officially partnered with British Petroleum (BP) to bolster cooperation in oil and natural gas projects in Kirkuk oilfields.

In 2025, BP reached a deal with Iraq’s North Oil Company (NOC) to develop oil fields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk, with investments projected to reach $25 billion.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s attempts to optimize energy sector investments, increase oil output, and minimize gas flaring.

The enhanced output directly addresses the Iraqi government’s growing deficit as a result of continued maritime restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

By producing more petroleum from Kirkuk, Baghdad reduces internal shipping expenses from southern fields while increasing supplies to global markets via outlets on the Mediterranean.

World.title: Iraqi Prime Minister orders higher military readiness as security tensions rise
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces Ali Al-Zaidi has directed all security and military formations to raise their operational readiness and combat preparedness, according to the Security Media Cell.

The directive aims to maintain a high state of preparedness across Iraq’s security forces through intensified training exercises and operational movements designed to strengthen national security and protect public interests.

In a statement, the Security Media Cell said the Commander-in-Chief instructed security and military forces to increase their level of readiness while conducting training exercises and field movements.

The measures are intended to ensure that all security formations remain fully prepared to carry out their assigned duties and respond to potential security developments.

According to the statement, the directive is part of ongoing efforts to maintain continuous operational readiness across Iraq’s armed forces.

The Security Media Cell said the enhanced readiness program is designed to reinforce Iraq’s security framework and improve the capabilities of military and security units.

Officials stated that maintaining high readiness contributes to:

Strengthening national security.

Preserving public stability.

Protecting Iraqi citizens.

Safeguarding public institutions and national interests.

The government has increasingly emphasized preparedness amid evolving regional security challenges.

The announcement comes during a period of elevated security concerns in Iraq following recent regional developments and heightened tensions involving armed groups.

The official statement, however, does not specify any particular threat or military operation linked to the readiness order.

Some media reports and political analysts have suggested the move may be connected to broader security developments or precautionary planning ahead of upcoming government deadlines. These assessments are analytical interpretations and were not included in the official Security Media Cell statement.

The latest directive reflects Baghdad’s continued focus on ensuring the operational effectiveness of Iraq’s security institutions.

By ordering additional training activities and maintaining high alert levels, the government aims to preserve stability while ensuring security forces remain prepared to respond to any developments affecting the country’s security environment.

World.title: Iraqi Drilling Company completes well rehabilitation at West Qurna 1 oil field
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Drilling Company (IDC) has successfully completed the rehabilitation of oil well WQ1-132 at the West Qurna 1 oil field, marking another step in Iraq’s efforts to enhance oil production efficiency and support the long-term development of its energy sector.

The project was carried out as part of the company’s operational program to improve well performance and maintain sustainable crude oil production.

According to a statement issued by the Iraqi Drilling Company, the rehabilitation work was completed in line with directives from Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair Al-Abadi and under the supervision of the company’s Director General, Mohammed Hantoosh Asad Al-Azirjawi.

Technical and engineering teams carried out the operation using the company’s specialized expertise and equipment.

The company said the rehabilitation project forms part of its broader strategy to improve the efficiency of existing oil wells while supporting sustainable production across Iraq’s major oil fields.

Restoration work on producing wells helps maximize output, extend operational life, and improve field performance without the need for entirely new drilling operations.

The Iraqi Drilling Company emphasized that the successful completion of the project reflects the capabilities of its engineering and technical staff, who continue to execute specialized rehabilitation operations according to approved operational plans.

The company noted that relying on local expertise strengthens operational efficiency while supporting the continued development of Iraq’s oil infrastructure.

West Qurna 1 is one of Iraq’s largest producing oil fields and plays a significant role in the country’s crude oil output.

Ongoing rehabilitation and maintenance projects are designed to ensure production stability, improve operational reliability, and meet the technical requirements of field development programs.

The completion of well WQ1-132 is expected to contribute to maintaining efficient production operations within the field as Iraq continues investing in the modernization of its energy sector.

World.title: Iraqi PM, Kurdistan president discuss Erbil-Baghdad cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and the president of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Nechirvan Barzani, discussed on Wednesday the country’s political, economic, and security situation.

During their meeting in Baghdad, the two leaders indicated that it is important to boost cooperation between the federal government and the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) to enhance stability, address challenges, and serve the interests of the Iraqi people, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Al-Zaidi affirmed the government’s commitment to resolving outstanding issues in line with the constitution, preserving Iraq’s unity, and strengthening national partnership.

Barzani stated that it is important to continue dialogue between national parties. He added that the KRG supports the federal government’s efforts to enhance stability and promote national development.

The discussions focused on approaches to secure the success of the government’s national agenda.

This high-level meeting comes after al-Zaidi’s trips to Turkey and Iran, where he met top officials, and Barzani’s visit to Damascus, where he met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa.

World.title: Iraq wins legal case in Jordan for Samarra Pharmaceutical Company
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Justice has announced a legal victory before the Jordanian judiciary after securing a final court ruling in favor of the State Company for Drug Industries and Medical Appliances in Samarra, a subsidiary of the Ministry of Industry and Minerals.

The ruling requires a Jordanian company to pay financial compensation following a dispute over the supply of medical materials that failed to meet agreed specifications.

According to a statement from the Ministry of Justice, the ministry’s Legal Department successfully represented the Iraqi pharmaceutical company throughout all stages of the legal proceedings before Jordanian courts.

The case involved a supply contract under which the Jordanian company was expected to provide metal covers for medical supplies. However, the supplier allegedly delivered products that did not comply with the contractual specifications.

Director of the Legal Department, Haitham Mohi Radi, said the final judgment issued by the Jordanian Court of Cassation, and upheld by both the Court of Appeal and the Court of First Instance, ordered the Jordanian company to pay financial amounts to the Samarra-based pharmaceutical company.

The ruling concludes a lengthy legal process aimed at protecting the contractual rights of the Iraqi state-owned enterprise.

The Ministry of Justice described the outcome as an important achievement in safeguarding Iraq’s financial interests abroad.

Officials said the successful litigation reflects the ministry’s continued efforts to defend state institutions before international courts and judicial authorities while protecting public funds from contractual violations.

The ministry added that the case demonstrates the expertise and professionalism of Iraq’s legal teams in handling international commercial disputes.

By successfully pursuing the claim through multiple judicial levels in Jordan, the Legal Department reinforced Iraq’s commitment to enforcing contractual rights and ensuring accountability in cross-border commercial agreements.

The decision is expected to strengthen confidence in the government’s ability to defend the interests of Iraqi public institutions through legal channels.

World.title: Ammar Al-Hakim and Iranian Science Minister discuss academic cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The head of Iraq’s National State Forces Alliance, Ammar Al-Hakim, met with Iranian Minister of Science, Research and Technology Hossein Simaei Sarraf in Baghdad to discuss expanding academic cooperation between Iraq and Iran through university partnerships, knowledge exchange, and joint educational initiatives.

The meeting focused on strengthening higher education ties while emphasizing the role of universities in addressing labor market needs and societal challenges.

According to a statement released by Al-Hakim’s office, the two sides reviewed opportunities to deepen cooperation between Iraqi and Iranian universities by promoting twinning agreements, expanding academic collaboration, and exchanging expertise.

The discussions highlighted the importance of strengthening institutional relationships to support scientific research and educational development in both countries.

During the meeting, Al-Hakim stressed that university graduates should possess skills that match the demands of today’s job market.

He also urged academic institutions to prioritize scientific research that offers practical solutions to national challenges and contributes to sustainable development.

Al-Hakim emphasized the importance of equipping university students with strong scientific knowledge to prepare them for future professional opportunities.

The Iraqi political leader underscored the role of research institutions in supporting innovation and policymaking.

He noted that universities should focus on producing research capable of addressing economic, social, and developmental issues while enhancing academic excellence.

The discussion reflected a shared interest in strengthening educational cooperation as part of broader bilateral relations.

The meeting also touched on the annual Arbaeen pilgrimage, with Al-Hakim praising the hospitality shown by Iraqis toward visitors traveling to commemorate Imam Hussein.

He said the event demonstrates positive values of solidarity and cooperation, while calling for stronger ties between societies based on shared humanitarian and religious principles.

The visit concluded with discussions on enhancing educational cooperation alongside broader people-to-people engagement between Iraq and Iran.

World.title: Iraq’s State Administration Coalition warns armed groups after September 30
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s State Administration Coalition has reaffirmed its support for restricting all weapons to state control, warning that any armed activity outside the authority of the government after September 30, 2026, will be treated under the country’s Anti-Terrorism Law.

The position was announced following the coalition’s 37th regular meeting, hosted by Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi, with the participation of Iraq’s senior political and constitutional leaders.

According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office, the meeting brought together the President of the Republic, the Speaker of Parliament, the President of the Supreme Judicial Council, the President of the Kurdistan Region, and leaders of the State Administration Coalition.

Participants reviewed Iraq’s political, security, economic, and public service developments, as well as regional events and their impact on the country.

The coalition reiterated its backing for the government’s efforts to ensure that all weapons remain under state authority, in line with the government program approved by the Iraqi Parliament.

The coalition stressed that Iraqi territory must not be used as a launchpad for attacks against neighboring countries or for actions that could draw Iraq into regional conflicts.

It warned that individuals or groups engaging in such activities would be committing crimes that threaten national security.

According to the statement, after September 30, 2026, any armed activity conducted outside the state’s legal framework will be dealt with under Iraq’s Anti-Terrorism Law.

Officials also cited constitutional provisions prohibiting the formation of armed organizations outside the official security forces.

Prime Minister Al-Zaidi briefed coalition members on government efforts to strengthen security, improve public services, implement the ministerial program, and address Iraq’s financial and economic challenges.

The coalition emphasized the need to:

Maintain national security and stability.

Protect essential public services.

Diversify Iraq’s oil export routes.

Increase non-oil revenues.

Combat corruption, smuggling, and financial waste.

The meeting highlighted the government’s commitment to protecting citizens’ interests while strengthening economic resilience.

On regional affairs, coalition leaders expressed support for diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing tensions across the Middle East.

The meeting reaffirmed Iraq’s rejection of resolving disputes through military force and emphasized Baghdad’s willingness to play a constructive role in promoting dialogue between regional parties.

Participants also discussed border security, counterterrorism cooperation, combating drug trafficking and organized crime, and strengthening relations with neighboring and international partners based on mutual respect and national sovereignty.

At the conclusion of the meeting, the State Administration Coalition called for accelerating the completion of the government formation process and submitting the government’s official program to the Council of Representatives for discussion and approval.

The coalition said completing these constitutional steps remains essential for advancing Iraq’s political stability and governance agenda.

World.title: Iltija faces FIR, questioning over 'assault' on cop, accuses police of manhandling; Omar calls it 'fixed match'

locked up in a battle over allegations of assault and manhandling, chief minister

Iltija, who accused police of manhandling her during the Aug 4-5 protest in Kashmir on the anniversary of the abrogation of

, was Friday called to Kothibagh police station in Srinagar and questioned for nearly two hours over her alleged assault on a cop. Police have alleged that she bit the forearm of an officer during the protest, causing an injury.

When asked about PDP chief Mehbooba Muftiâs criticism of the action against her daughter, Omar told reporters: âPlease donât ask me to comment on this fixed match.

Whenever PDPâs political image weakens, agencies step in to help restore its credibility as they are the partyâs mai baap. This party didnât rise on its own, and it was made by agencies (a euphemism widely used by NC to refer to intelligence agencies).â

Questioning the claims and counter-claims, Omar said: âIs Iltija Mufti a five-year-old child that she would bite someone? This entire episode is a fixed match and an unnecessary attempt to distract people from the real issues.â





While police did not issue any statement on Iltijaâs questioning, she said she was willing to cooperate with any investigation. However, she added: âI am neither the first nor the last Kashmiri to be summoned. My fight is not personal. I am here to fight for every Kashmiri.â

World.title: Police put up posters of Lashkar commander across J&K, declare Rs 15L reward
World.content:
JAMMU: J&K Police have intensified the hunt for

World.title: 'Fake news, AI-generated': MEA dismisses report of India requesting defence pact with Israel after Mecca agreement
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Ministry of External Affairs on Friday rejected a report claiming India had approached Israel for a defence pact following the signing of a new security agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey.

The ministry called the claim âfake newsâ generated using artificial intelligence.

The report, published by Turkish outlet Straturka and subsequently circulated on social media, claimed that New Delhi had initiated discussions with Tel Aviv to counter the emerging Pakistan-Saudi-Turkey security arrangement. The report cited unnamed Pakistani sources.

The MEAâs Fact Check unit shared a screenshot of the report on X and flagged it as fake, warning users against what it described as malicious social media posts created using AI.

âWe caution against such malicious posts on social media platforms which use AI to create fake content!â the ministryâs Fact Check wing said.

The claim surfaced after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, which seeks to deepen military and security cooperation among the three countries. Pakistan has described the agreement as a collective-deterrence arrangement, with its foreign ministry saying an armed attack on any one of the three signatories would be treated as an attack on all three.

The agreement has drawn attention in New Delhi, with the MEA saying India is closely monitoring developments.

âWe are also closely following this development, and we shall keep you updated,â MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said at the ministryâs weekly briefing.

The MEAâs clarification came a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke by phone with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The two leaders discussed ways to further strengthen the India-Israel Special Strategic Partnership and reviewed cooperation between the two countries across several areas.

The conversation focused on strengthening bilateral ties and the existing partnership between India and Israel, rather than any new defence pact linked to the Pakistan-Saudi-Turkey agreement.

World.title: India counters China's 'map war', assigns official names to 27 Arunachal sites
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India has formally identified 27 locations in Arunachal Pradesh by their standard names on the official map of the country, a move that comes amid China's repeated attempts to rename places in the border state.

The government said the exercise is intended to ensure the correct identification of these places and improve public awareness of their geographical and historical significance.

"Identifying them formally on the Survey of India map of Arunachal Pradesh is aimed at facilitating their accurate recognition and better awareness among the public at large," an official statement said.

New Delhi has consistently rejected Beijing's practice of assigning Chinese names to places in Arunachal Pradesh, describing the exercise as "vain and preposterous".

India has maintained that such actions do not change the "undeniable" fact that the state "was, is, and will" remain an integral part of the country.

Several of the newly marked locations hold strategic importance because of their proximity to the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and their role in past India-China military confrontations.

Among them is Long Ju, one of the earliest flashpoints between the two countries.





Chinese troops entered the area in 1959, years before the 1962 war.

The official map also includes Maja village in Upper Subansiri district near Long Ju, Bisa village and the strategically significant mountain passes of Dzo La, Riza La and Pukur La.

Another key location is Thag La, the high-altitude pass where one of the opening battles of the 1962 India-China war took place.

Jairampur in Changlang district has also been formally identified.

The town serves as an important logistics hub for the movement of security forces towards eastern Arunachal Pradesh and the Myanmar border.

Other locations added to the map include the high-altitude lake Sambho Sarovar, Bara Kundun, Chhota Kundun, Dhan Bari, Pritnagar, Teritnagar, Ramnagar, Jaswant Garh, Sagar, Padma, Jyotinagar, Baisakhi, Sher-e-Thapa Memorial, Chhota Ropuk, Bara Ropuk, Shivaji Nagar, Sunpura, Kamlang Nagar and Buddhamandir.

Jaswant Garh commemorates Indian Army soldier

, while the Sher-e-Thapa Memorial honours 1962 war hero Trilok Singh Thapa.

India has repeatedly dismissed China's attempts to assign what it calls "fictitious names" to places in Arunachal Pradesh, saying such efforts seek to create "baseless narratives" and cannot alter the "undeniable" reality on the ground. New Delhi has also warned that such actions could undermine efforts to improve bilateral ties.

China first issued a list of six standardised names for places in what it calls Zangnan in 2017. It followed this with a second list covering 15 locations in 2021 and another naming 11 places in 2023. Beijing uses the name Zangnan to refer to Arunachal Pradesh, a claim India has consistently rejected.

World.title: Jharkhand government holds talks with protesting students, promises to consider demands
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Jharkhand government on Friday said it was ready to consider the demands of protesting students after a delegation of ministers met representatives of the JPSC/JSSC Reforms Manch.

According to the students' delegation, the meeting was held in a positive atmosphere, with the government assuring them that their demands would be considered.

"We met the delegation of student protesters. The government is ready to consider their demands sympathetically," Jharkhand minister Sudivya Kumar said after the meeting.

The talks came as the government sought to resolve the ongoing agitation over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations.

According to the JPSC/JSSC Reforms Manch, four of the five members of the government's panel - ministers Sudivya Kumar, Dipika Pandey Singh, Chamra Linda and Sanjay Prasad Yadav - attended the meeting.

The protesters have been demanding the cancellation of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Examination and an independent probe into the alleged irregularities, either by the CBI or by a panel of retired high court judges from outside the state.

Earlier, the protesting students submitted a fresh 10-member panel to the state government for talks after the government objected to the previous 11-member panel, which included an advocate and two technical experts, the Manch said.

World.title: National Handloom Day: Yogi Adityanath salutes artisans, recalls Swadeshi Movement's legacy
World.content:
Marking National Handloom Day, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister

on Thursday paid tribute to the State's weaving community, describing handloom artisans as preservers of India's cultural heritage and emphasising their role in carrying forward traditions that have been passed down through generations.

Addressing a gathering in Lucknow after presenting the Sant Kabir State-Level Handloom Awards, the Chief Minister congratulated artisans across the State and linked the occasion to India's freedom movement.

"Today is National Handloom Day. I congratulate all the artisans across the state on Handloom Day. It was on this very day, August 7, 1905, that India's freedom struggle received a new direction," Adityanath said.

He recalled that August 7 commemorates the launch of the Swadeshi Movement, which encouraged Indians to embrace indigenous products and reject foreign goods during the freedom struggle. According to the Chief Minister, the movement not only strengthened the spirit of self-reliance but also boosted confidence in India's traditional industries, particularly handloom weaving.

The Chief Minister said the handloom sector is more than an economic activity.





It represents India's identity, craftsmanship and cultural continuity. He stated that every handwoven fabric carries the story of the artisan behind it and reflects centuries of skill, patience and creativity.

Uttar Pradesh is home to several renowned handloom traditions, including the Banarasi silk saree, Chikankari embroidery of Lucknow, Bhadohi carpets and handwoven textiles from Mau, Tanda and Mubarakpur.

These crafts provide livelihoods to thousands of weaving families and contribute significantly to the state's economy and exports.

Adityanath said recognising artisans through state-level awards is an effort to encourage excellence while inspiring younger generations to preserve traditional crafts. He added that supporting weavers through government initiatives, better market access and modern technology is a priority.

National Handloom Day is observed every year on August 7 to commemorate the Swadeshi Movement launched in 1905. The day celebrates India's rich handloom heritage and honours millions of weavers whose craftsmanship continues to keep traditional textile arts alive despite changing market trends and industrialisation.

World.title: Watch: Delhi-NCR drowns in rain chaos; 7 videos show waterlogging, gridlock

NEW DELHI: Heavy rainfall lashed several parts of Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR) on Friday, leading to widespread waterlogging, traffic congestion and disruptions to vehicular movement during peak hours.

The IMD issued a red alert, forecasting moderate rain at many places and heavy rain at isolated locations accompanied by moderate thunderstorms and lightning over the next few hours. According to the weather office, Safdarjung recorded 59.2 mm of rainfall till 8.30am, while Lodhi Road received 60.4 mm, Ridge 57 mm, Ayanagar 26.2 mm and Palam 16.9 mm.

The IMD has forecast light to moderate rainfall over Delhi till August 10.

World.title: Past tense, eye on future: Air India hikes pilots’ pay by 8% to 15%
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Air India on Friday hiked pilot salaries by 8% to 15%, with commanders getting the biggest hikes and then the same tapering with rank. Going ahead, first officers or co-pilots will primarily get command upgrade (become captains) in AI Express (which has only single aisles) and then move to AI (which has wide body aircraft too that have higher pay) for a âstrong foundation for progression within the groupâ.

The group has tried to do multiple things â make AI Express more attractive for pilots through better pay and address shortage there mainly on the Boeing 737 fleet; check resignations and retain cockpit crew.

AI pilots have for years been facing a 40 hour guaranteed pay â meaning they will get minimum for these many hours irrespective of actual flying and flying more will for more pay â while IndiGo has fixed pay for 70 hours.

This has been a cause of heartburn among pilots. Under the revised framework while AI will continue to provide guaranteed pay for 40 flying hours but has enhanced flying allowance rates. Flying allowance rates beyond 40 hours have also been increased, aligning compensation with industry benchmarks while rewarding productivity.

Now AI is restoring international flights that were slashed post the West Asia crisis and will return to Jan-Feb level by next month.





The constraint of Pakistan airspace closure remains for Indian carriers and the longer routes they have to take for flying to and from the west â unlike direct routes taken by foreign carriers â means higher flying time and greater pilot requirement.

Now a senior commander flying for about 55 hours in a month will get Rs 8.3 lakh, up from Rs 7.5 lakh at present. And a first officer doing so will get Rs 3.3 lakh, up from just over Rs 3 lakh as of now.

While privilege leave has been reduced from 30 to 24, the airline will not be counting mandatory weekly off time pilots get as per regulatory requirement and the new leave structure accounts does not factor that which comes across as a cut in leave, said people in the know. IndiGo may relook at its leave policy too for pilots.

Since Tata Group took over AI and AI Express in Jan 2022, the Maharaja has lost over Rs 55,000 crore due to multiple factors.

The pilot pay hike announced Friday indicates it is looking at the future and preparing for growth with hundreds of aircraft on order without being bogged down by the tumultuous recent past.

âNew career pathways, enhanced compensation and benefits, and improved quality-of-life initiatives support Air India Group's next phase of expansion. At the heart of these initiatives is a clear, structured and transparent career pathway that provides faster command opportunities, long-term progression and access to one of the most significant widebody growth programmes in global aviation,â said an official.

Since 2022, AI Group has grown from around 100 aircraft to nearly 300 aircraft and has placed orders for 600 new aircraft, including 80 wide body aircraft. Tatas are investing in capability building, including the establishment of a modern aviation academy in Gurugram with Airbus and Boeing full-flight simulators, and a new flying training school in Amravati, Maharashtra.

âAs AI group expands, it is focused on developing and retaining internal talent through a structured progression model across Air India Express and Air India.

Pilots across Air India and Air India Express will operate under a common seniority framework, creating an integrated and transparent pathway for career progression across the group. This framework provides greater visibility into future opportunities while ensuring a consistent and structured approach to advancement,â said teh official.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Under the new framework, AI Express will serve as âthe primary pathway for pilots seeking command upgrades.

This approach is designed to accelerate command opportunities, enable pilots to build command experience earlier in their careers, and create a strong foundation for progression within the Group.â

Following command experience at AI Express, pilots will have the opportunity to progress to Air India and subsequently pursue widebody flying and command opportunities. âWith 80 additional widebody aircraft on order and scheduled for induction over the coming years, Air India offers pilots a long-term pathway that is unique in the Indian market,â the official said. An additional incentive is being offered to pilots who sign up to support the growing Boeing 737 fleet in Air India Express under which they will receive a fleet allowance.

World.title: India has sent ‘formal’ invite to Nepal PM Balendra Shah: MEA
World.content:
India has ‘formally’ invited Nepal’s new Prime Minister Balendra Shah to visit New Delhi, the Ministry of External Affairs said on Tuesday (July 28, 2026).

This official confirmation comes days after sections of the Nepali media reported that Mr. Shah’s advisor Kumar Ben visited New Delhi in early July and discussed the Nepali PM’s visit with National Security Advisor Ajit Doval.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi had congratulated the newly elected PM of Nepal on social media soon after Mr. Shah swept the polls in March. In his message, Mr. Modi had said, “Your appointment reflects the trust reposed in your leadership by the people of Nepal. I look forward to working closely with you to take India-Nepal friendship and cooperation to even greater heights for the mutual benefit of our two peoples.”

“We have invited Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah formally,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, in response to a question from The Hindu on Tuesday (July 28, 2026). Officials said that Mr. Modi’s remark was the beginning of the process and the formal invitation was subsequently sent to Mr. Shah through proper diplomatic channels.

Evolving relationship

Following the victory of Mr. Shah’s Rastriya Swatantra Party, there were reports that Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri was expected to visit Kathmandu in May but the visit did not take place as Mr. Shah had declined to engage with visiting high level foreign bureaucrats, insisting that he would meet his political counterparts in other countries.

The first high-profile visit was by Nepal’s Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal on June 6 and 7. Mr. Khanal had been scheduled to attend the Big Cat Alliance meeting planned to be held in Delhi on the sidelines of the India-Africa Forum Summit. After that meeting was postponed due to an Ebola virus outbreak in Africa, however, Mr. Khanal stayed for a bilateral visit. India also hosted Rabi Lamichhane, chairman of the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party, in the first week of June.

Reports from Kathmandu had earlier suggested that Mr. Shah had taken a vow not to visit foreign destinations after coming to power, saying his focus would be limited to domestic priorities in the initial phase of his government’s tenure.

woAt the same time, however, he raised the Kalapani-Lipulekh-Limpiyadhura territorial dispute with India in a statement in the Nepali parliament, saying that Nepal is in talks with the United Kingdom regarding the historical documents necessary to research the dispute. He also sought talks with China on that issue.

World.title: SCoR honours four employees with safety awards
World.content:
South Coast Railway (SCoR) General Manager Sandeep Mathur on Tuesday presented Safety Awards to four employees for exemplary vigilance and timely intervention in averting potential accidents.

This marks the inaugural presentation of Safety Awards by the General Manager since the formation of the South Coast Railway zone.

M. Ramesh Babu, station superintendent at Chirala in the Vijayawada Division, was honoured for his alertness on June 2, 2026. While exchanging signals with an Up Goods train, he noticed broken iron strips securing iron coil rolls on two wagons. His prompt communication with the loco pilot and control office ensured the train was halted at Vetapalem, preventing potential obstruction and derailment risks on adjacent tracks.

Shivam Dixit, pointsman at Yerpedu in the Guntakal Division, was recognised for detecting a slack fish plate and a weld crack on the Down Main Line within the Yerpedu Yard late at night on June 15, 2026. His immediate notification to station authorities enabled swift engineering intervention.

M. Praveen Kumar, senior assistant loco pilot from Guntakal, was commended for spotting a red-hot wheel on a passing freight rake while operating Train No. B-15 on June 1, 2026. His quick use of the walkie-talkie and alerting the opposing crew, lead to a timely stop and detection of a hot axle at Bantanahal.

Ch. Ram Mohan Rao, train manager from the Visakhapatnam Division, was felicitated for observing a hot axle on an adjacent Up Goods train while working the Yesvantpur–Howrah Express (Train No. 12864) on May 9, 2026. His relay of information to the coaching controller and Vizianagaram station enabled carriage and wagon staff to promptly rectify the mechanical defect.

General Manager Sandeep Mathur lauded their dedication and high sense of responsibility. He emphasised that the proactive observation of frontline staff remains the bedrock of safe, secure, and reliable railway operations.

World.title: Breastfeeding awareness programme held at MGM Healthcare
World.content:
MGM Healthcare organised a breastfeeding awareness programme in Chennai on Friday, as part of World Breastfeeding Week, bringing together over 100 lactating mothers and healthcare professionals.

Veteran actor Radhika Sarathkumar participated in the programme, which brought together paediatricians, neonatologists, obstetricians, gynaecologists and lactation consultants to address concerns and dispel myths related to breastfeeding.

The week-long programme included poster and rangoli competitions, a reels competition for lactating mothers and a well-baby contest based on exclusive breastfeeding practices. An interactive session with specialists was also held to discuss breastfeeding-related concerns.

According to the press release, MGM Healthcare Managing Director Urjitha Rajagopalan said the hospital encouraged mothers to breastfeed for at least a year and provided support and guidance. Chandra Kumar, Senior Consultant and Head of Paediatrics and Neonatology, said exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months is important for an infant’s nutrition, immunity and development.

The programme was organised by the hospital’s Paediatrics and Neonatology and Obstetrics and Gynaecology departments under its ‘Varam’ initiative.

World.title: T.N. Housing Minister to inaugurate The Hindu Real Estate & Infrastructure Summit 2026 on July 30
World.content:
Rapidly expanding city infrastructure, urbanisation, and the rise of integrated communities has led to a recent increase in demand from both end-users and investors in Chennai. With the city’s real estate sector entering a definitive growth phase, The Hindu is organising The Real Estate & Infrastructure Summit 2026, presented by Casagrand in association with Adissia Developers, on July 30 at ITC Grand Chola, Chennai.

The summit will be inaugurated by Tamil Nadu’s Minister for Housing and Urban Development B. Rajkumar, who will deliver the keynote address on the future of urban development and infrastructure in India. The event will serve as a platform for developers, investors, architects, urban planners, technology experts, and policymakers to exchange ideas on the opportunities and challenges emerging across the real estate and infrastructure sectors.

The summit will feature keynote addresses and discussions by prominent voices from the real estate and infrastructure sectors, including M.N. Arun, managing director, Casagrand; M.V. Manikandan, founder and CMD, Adissia Developers; and members of CREDAI Chennai.

Urban real estate trends

Business leaders and experts are expected to examine the most significant trends transforming India’s urban landscape, such as the rapid expansion of Global Capability Centres (GCCs), rise of smart manufacturing hubs, growing role of artificial intelligence in construction, emergence of new investment corridors, and the luxury housing boom. Other sessions will focus on sustainable housing, policy reforms, and the capital flows driving the country’s next phase of urban growth.

The summit aims to facilitate meaningful networking among industry stakeholders, offering participants an opportunity to engage directly with the decision-makers expected to shape India’s real estate and infrastructure landscape over the coming decade.

Associate Partners: Navin’s and Mindspace REIT; Banking Partner: State Bank of India; Insurance Partner: United India Insurance; Academic Partner: Saveetha College of Architecture & Design; Industry Partner: CREDAI Chennai; Television Partner: Puthiya Thalaimurai; Digital News Partner: The Federal. Participation is by invitation only. Those interested may register by visiting https://newsth.live/THRES2026 or by scanning the QR code.

World.title: Police arrest two youths for selling ganja, Tapentadol tablets
World.content:
Two youths were arrested for allegedly possessing and selling ganja and Tapentadol tablets during a special anti-narcotics drive conducted by Old Guntur police on Tuesday. Police seized 1.1 kg of ganja, 90 Tapentadol tablets and ₹9,000 in cash from their possession.

Guntur Superintendent of Police (SP) Vakul Jindal, in a press release on Tuesday, said that acting on specific information, a police team led by Old Guntur Circle Inspector (CI) Venkata Prasad, under the supervision of East DSP T. Seetharam, conducted a raid in Old Guntur police station limits.

The accused were identified as Sheikh Mastan (25) of Anandpet and Sheikh Mastan alias Munna (27) of Allinagar, both residents of Guntur. During questioning, the accused allegedly confessed that they had procured ganja and Tapentadol tablets through an associate identified as Bilal, who reportedly brought the contraband from Goa. They allegedly packed the ganja into small sachets and sold them along with the tablets for profit.

A case has been registered and further investigation is under way to trace the supplier and identify others involved in the network.

The SP commended East DSP T. Seetharam, CI Venkata Prasad and the police team for successfully detecting the case and strengthening the district’s ongoing crackdown on narcotics.

World.title: Does digital arrest need to be made a ‘standalone offence’: Supreme Court
World.content:
The Supreme Court asked on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) whether digital arrest and related cyber crimes should be made a “standalone offence” and assets of people running these scams seized.

“Do we need to formally define digital arrest or related cyber crimes in the penal law? There are ingredients of robbery, extortion, dacoity… everything is there. Do you need it to define it as a standalone offence?” Chief Justice Surya Kant, heading a three-judge Bench, asked Attorney-General R. Venkataramani, appearing for the Union government.

Mr. Venkataramani said the offences were already covered in the existing penal laws.

The court went further to ask if the assets of those under investigation should be seized if a prima facie offence was made out against them.

The Chief Justice had previously flagged digital arrest scams as the “most disturbing” among cybercrimes, which not only result in “financial loss” to victims but also a “blistering sense of violation”. The CJI had said cybercrimes like digital arrests must not be seen as mere economic offences, but an offence against human dignity.

Records submitted by the Home Ministry in the court in April showed over 2.41 lakh complaints related to digital arrest scams alone.

The court had suo motu taken cognisance of digital arrests scams in January this year, saying that victims were psychologically coerced by fraudsters dressed up convincingly as police officers and judicial officers to cough up huge sums of their savings to avert fictional arrests or punitive action.

World.title: Child rights panel resolves 46 complaints
World.content:
The Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights resolved as many as 46 complaints during its sitting held in Ernakulam. A total of 54 complaints were considered, while eight others were set aside to be taken up later.

Commission members K.K. Shaju and T.C. Jalaja Mol led the proceedings. The panel expressed concern over the rising incidence of child rights violations among school students. The Commission members noted that there was a need to provide training to teachers and parents regarding child rights laws.

The Commission considered a request submitted by a school leader to ensure the safety of children who required special attention and protection at an upper primary school in the district. The Commission members said the complaint was resolved with the cooperation of the District Child Protection Officer and the Department of Women and Child Development.

World.title: UDF names V.R. Sudheer as nominee for Kochi Corporation deputy mayor election
World.content:
Four-time councillor V.R. Sudheer has been named as the United Democratic Front (UDF) candidate for the deputy mayor’s election of the Kochi Corporation, scheduled for Wednesday.

A meeting of the Congress Parliamentary Party, chaired by District Congress Committee (DCC) president Mohammed Shiyas, MLA, on Tuesday unanimously selected Mr. Sudheer, who represents the Elamakkara South division. The post fell vacant after incumbent Deepak Joy resigned on May 13, shortly after being elected as Thripunithura MLA. It has remained vacant since, drawing criticism from the Opposition Left Democratic Front (LDF), which alleged an administrative impasse as the deputy mayor also chairs the crucial finance standing committee of the Corporation.

The LDF has fielded P.J. Yesudas, representing the Nasrathu division, while first-time councillor Jalaja S. Acharya, representing Thrikkanarvattom, will contest for the BJP. The outcome is expected to be a foregone conclusion, given that the UDF enjoys the support of 48 members, including one Independent, in the 76-member house, while the LDF and the BJP have 22 and six members respectively.

The Congress had earlier allotted split terms of two-and-a-half years each to Mr. Joy and K.V.P. Krishnakumar, representing the ‘A’ and ‘I’ factions respectively. A similar arrangement is in place for the Mayor’s post, with Congress councillors V.K. Minimol and Shiny Mathew sharing the position.

Though several names within the ‘A’ faction were initially considered, Mr. Sudheer remained the frontrunner throughout owing to his seniority.

World.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye sign tripartite defence agreement in Makkah
World.content:
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Friday signed a joint defence pact in Makkah that empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, which seeks to strengthen the collective security of the three states, was signed by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince and PM Mohammad bin Salman, and Türkiye’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the “Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence” held at Al-Safa Palace.

The three countries announced the signing of the agreement in a joint statement published by the Foreign Office (FO) and Saudi Arabia’s official SPA press agency.

The statement said the pact reflected the three countries’ “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond, in pursuit of a secure and prosperous future”.

“The agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression, and stipulates that any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all.”

It also “provides for the enhancement of all aspects of defence cooperation” among the three countries, the statement added.

The agreement is “guided by the longstanding historical ties among the three states, based on the enduring bonds of brotherhood and Islamic solidarity that unite them, and building upon their shared strategic interests and longstanding defence cooperation”.

During the Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence, the “distinguished relations” between the three countries were reviewed, “along with a number of issues of mutual interest”, the statement noted.

Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif were also present at the signing ceremony.

The defence and foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Turkiye were in attendance as well, pictures showed.

Sealing the agreement in Makkah, the holiest site in Islam, adds symbolic heft to a pact that builds on longstanding bilateral military ties among the three countries.

The agreement ties together Pakistan, the only nuclear-armed Muslim country; Saudi Arabia, the home to Islam’s holiest sites and one of the world’s top oil exporters; and Turkiye, Nato’s second-largest military.

‘Shield of peace’

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif described the signing of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement as a “historic pact”, saying the three countries were united by faith, friendship and a shared commitment to peace and security.

In a post on X, the prime minister said he was honoured to sign the agreement alongside the Saudi crown prince and the Turkish president.

He said the pact would serve as a “shield of peace” for generations and expressed hope that it would bring prosperity to the three countries and the wider Muslim world. Shehbaz also appreciated Field Marshal Asim Munir’s efforts and dedication towards the agreement.

‘Historic day for Pakistan’

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, while talking to a private TV channel, described the signing of the joint defence agreement between the three states as a “historic day” for Pakistan, saying the pact reflected growing recognition of the country’s defence capabilities and strengthened ties among the three nations.

Speaking about the agreement, Tarar said the defence cooperation framework would take relations between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye to a new level. He credited Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir with bringing the three countries together, saying they had an “ideal working relationship” and that their teamwork had contributed to recent successes.

Tarar said the agreement was aimed at strengthening defence cooperation and served as a form of deterrence rather than aggression. The minister further said Pakistan’s capabilities had been demonstrated during last year’s conflict with India and claimed that the country had since played a role in promoting regional peace.

Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan said that the signing of the joint defence agreement by the crown prince, the president of Türkiye and the prime minister of Pakistan underscored the depth of the fraternal and strategic relations between the three countries.

He said the agreement marked an important milestone in their defence cooperation and reflected their shared desire to coordinate efforts to address challenges and threats affecting regional security and stability. He added that the pact embodied the three countries’ shared political will to safeguard security, support a more secure regional environment and pave the way for greater development and prosperity.

Saudi Arabia’s Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said the agreement “does not represent an effort to establish a military axis or a sectarian bloc”.

“Nor is it linked to any nuclear ambitions or arms race; rather, it is focused on building sustainable capabilities,” he wrote on X.

He noted that the deal “does not constitute a threat to the security of any country in the region, nor does it represent an escalation of tensions between any two states”.

The Saudi official further said the agreement “does not supersede or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between these countries”.

Mansoor Ahmed, of the Australian National University’s Strategic and Defence Studies Centre, said Islamabad and Ankara bring strong defence industries to the table, while Riyadh could contribute with technological spending.

While the pact comes in the backdrop of the US-Israel war on Iran, Bloomberg had reported in January — before the conflict began — that Ankara was seeking to join a separate mutual defence pact between Islamabad and Riyadh.

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both.

In January, Reuters quoted Defence Production Minister Raza Hayat Harraj as saying that a draft had been prepared after 10 months of talks. Turkish FM Hakan Fidan had said Ankara favoured an “inclusive platform that creates wider, bigger cooperation and stability”.

Pakistan has also sought to mediate efforts to end the US-Iran war, while Turkiye has played a diplomatic role in negotiations aimed at ending the war in Gaza.

The three countries, along with Egypt, have been closely involved in efforts to promote regional stability and contain the regional upheaval sparked by the US-Iran war.

The regional conflagration has rained missile fire onto Gulf oil exporters, with Iran targeting Gulf countries in retaliation for attacks carried out against it using US military bases in the region.

The deal also comes as a 2022 truce between Riyadh and the Houthi rebels in Yemen has broken down.

After the two sides traded fire for the first time in years last month, Houthis declared a maritime blockade against the kingdom, threatening access to its ports, and has claimed to have attacked Saudi tankers in the Red Sea.

Pakistan had condemned the Houthis’ threats to Saudi Arabia and to trading with the kingdom via the Red Sea. It also warned that it had the right to self-defence if its “maritime interests” were targeted in “any hostile act”.

As the conflict expanded onto new fronts, Saudi Arabia last week unveiled plans for a multinational maritime defence coalition to protect shipping and energy supply routes in the Red Sea. Fourteen countries, including Pakistan, have voiced support for the coalition.

Saudi crown prince meets PM Shehbaz, Erdogan

Crown Prince Salman held separate meetings with PM Shehbaz and President Erdogan at the Al-Safa Palace earlier in the day.

DPM Dar, CDF Munir and Asif were also present in the meeting with PM Shehbaz, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said.

Meanwhile, Erdogan’s office confirmed on X that he also held a meeting with Crown Prince Salman.

PM Shehbaz arrived in Saudi Arabia on a three-day visit on Thursday, while the Turkish president undertook a one-day visit today, Anadolu Agency reported.

Erdogan landed at King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah, from where he departed for Makkah by road, the Turkish news outlet reported.

PM Shehbaz had landed in Jeddah on Thursday. CDF Munir later joined the Pakistani delegation, which also included Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and Special Assistant to PM Tariq Fatemi.

On Friday morning, the delegation visited the Holy Kaaba and performed Umrah, the PMO said. PM Shehbaz is also expected to visit Masjid-i-Nabvi (PBUH) in Madina.

According to an earlier statement by the FO, discussions between the two sides were to “focus on consolidating the Pakistan-Saudi bilateral relations as well as exchange of views on regional and international developments of mutual interests”.

The FO had noted that although the visit was taking place amid heightened tensions in the Gulf, it carries “significance beyond the immediate crises and short-term considerations”.

It said the visit will “further strengthen bilateral relations, deepen strategic cooperation, enhance coordination on regional and international issues of mutual interest, and reinforce multilateral cooperation”.

“The visit marks Pakistan’s long-standing partnership with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia anchored in decades of mutual trust, cooperation and brotherhood,” the FO had emphasised.

Pakistan has provided training and technical assistance to Saudi forces for decades, while Turkiye and Pakistan have exchanged warships and training aircraft.

In 2023, Riyadh agreed to buy Turkish drones in what Ankara called its largest defence export contract. In April this year, Saudi Arabia said it received a military force and fighter jets from Pakistan to boost the kingdom’s security.

Additional input from AFP and Reuters

World.title: Goods transporters to go on strike from Saturday after talks with govt fail
World.content:
Goods transporters and oil tanker operators began suspending their services on Friday night after negotiations with the government failed, ahead of their nationwide wheel-jam strike scheduled for Saturday.

All Pakistan Goods Transport Itehad spokesman and All Pakistan Goods Transport Owners Association President Mohammad Owais Chaudhry Advocate told Dawn that talks with Federal Minister for Communications Aleem Khan and other government officials had failed.

He said the negotiations ended without a breakthrough, prompting transporters, including edible oil tanker operators, petroleum oil tanker operators, truckers, trailer operators and other intercity transporters, to proceed with their previously announced strike.

“We have informed the government side about the problems we are facing and our concerns,” Chaudhry said, adding that the strike would continue until their demands were accepted.

However, the minister has assured the transporters that he would discuss their demands, and the next round of talks would be held on Monday morning.

The unified body of transporters had already announced that it would begin its wheel-jam strike from August 8, and warned that it would not be a token strike but an indefinite one.

“Commercial goods carriers across the country have already been taken off the roads and will remain stationed at designated places during the protest period,” Chaudhry said.

Among the key demands of the transporters is the uniform enforcement of axle-load limits across the country and permission for 10-wheel vehicles to carry up to 35 tonnes.

They have also demanded reductions in diesel prices and toll taxes, besides seeking relief in withholding tax to ease the financial burden on the transport sector.

The transporters have also called for the withdrawal of customs provisions that, according to the association, allow authorities to confiscate vehicles carrying goods found to be in violation of customs laws.

Other demands include the withdrawal of the Punjab Highway Patrol’s powers to issue challans to commercial vehicles, an end to what the association described as unnecessary challans and excessive fines on motorways and highways, and measures to facilitate the issuance of heavy transport vehicle licences to drivers.

World.title: Sindh govt constitutes third medical board for exhumation of Mir Ali Raza’s body
World.content:
After withdrawing its two earlier notifications, the Sindh government on Friday notified a newly constituted eight-member medical board to carry out the exhumation of 25-year-old business owner Mir Ali Raza’s body on Saturday.

The exhumation, which was originally scheduled for Friday, was deferred after the deceased’s family objected to the abrupt reconstitution of the medical board, just hours after the notification of the first one.

A notification issued by the Sindh Health Department on Friday named police surgeon Dr Sumaiyya Syed as the convener of the board and Dow University of Health Sciences (DUHS) Pathology Department head Professor Dr Naseem Ahmed as the pathologist.

The eight-member board also includes Jinnah Sindh Medical University’s (JSMU) Dr Farah Waseem as a forensic expert, Shanakht Project’s Amir Hassan Khan as a forensic identification expert, Additional Police Surgeon Dr Srichand, Jinnah Post-Graduate Medical Centre (JPMC) medicolegal officers Dr Kamran Khan and Dr Daniyal Mirza, and Office of Police Surgeon Administrative In-charge Dr Muhammad.

According to the notification, the board may also co-opt any expert member if required.

Moreover, a notification issued by the Office of the Police Surgeon said that the exhumation of Ali’s body would be carried out on Saturday, August 8, at 11am. A civil judge and judicial magistrate Karachi-XXI would also be present, according to the police surgeon’s office.

Reconstitution of board

On Thursday, a Karachi court allowed the exhumation of Ali’s body on an application filed by the victim’s father, directing the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medico-legal board for the exhumation of Ali’s body “at the earliest possible date and time”.

The court ruling came after a controversy emerged between the Karachi police surgeon and investigators over alleged loopholes in the medico-legal report regarding the post-mortem examination.

The Sindh Health Department then constituted the eight-member board, with the police surgeon as the convener. Dr Ahmed of Dow DUHS, Dr Waseem of JSMU, Amir Khan of Citizens Police Liaison Committee, Dr Sirichand, Dr Kamran and Dr Daniyal of JPCM and Dr Yaseen, the admin in-charge of the police surgeon’s office, were the other members of the board.

However, a new order had been issued by the Sindh Health Directorate. The notification said that the board had been reconstituted to conduct the exhumation and medico-legal examination of the deceased.

While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new board, its members were changed to Prof Dr Zakiuddin from DUHS, Prof Dr Kazi Akbar and Prof Dr Abid Hussain Chang from Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences and Hyderabad Police Surgeon Dr Waseem Khan.

Controversy over autopsy

Raza, owner of eatery Wafflix, had gone missing on July 28. The 25-year-old’s body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Gulistan-i-Jauhar.

Initially, on the complaint lodged by his father, a case was registered at the Ferozabad police station under Section 365 (kidnapping or abducting with intent secretly and wrongfully to confine a person) of the Pakistan Penal Code.

Police maintain that the investigation has revealed that Ali had been facing financial difficulties and had asked his friends for money the night he died.

According to police, he had left his home in PECHS Block-2 and hired a taxi through an app. The taxi driver dropped him a short distance from the spot where his body was found, police said.

The case took a new turn when Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed told a private news channel on Tuesday that the postmortem findings of Ali’s body had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs.

She said the reported entry wound, bullet trajectory and exit wound did not correspond with one another. While it was scientifically possible for a bullet to enter through the back and exit from the front, she stressed that her assessment was based only on the postmortem report and photographs, as she had not examined the body herself.

The police surgeon noted that entry wounds were typically smaller than exit wounds in firearm cases. She also said that gunshot residue, commonly found on the hands in suspected suicides, was not tested for in this case.

Her interview prompted the police authorities to issue a statement, terming such observations as having the potential to adversely affect the ongoing investigation.

The statement, however, said that exhumation of the dead body could be done on the medical board’s recommendation for further clarification by a committee of medico-legal experts with the court’s permission.

World.title: Bilawal claims 'certain elements' within PML-N are sowing division among allies, undermining PM Shehbaz
World.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari claimed on Friday that certain elements within the ruling PML-N were undermining Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and sowing discord between him and his political allies.

The PPP and the PML-N have been engaged in a war of words since the latter emerged in the lead in Mirpur polls on July 27. The PML-N has also won the majority of the seats in the second phase , with the PPP accusing it of rigging and other violent tactics in both phases.

The PPP chief was addressing an election rally in Azad Jammu and Kashmir’s Poonch district, where the third phase of elections in the region is slated to be held.

“High-profile people are saying that the government has collapsed. I’m not saying that, nor am I casting doubt on the prime minister’s intentions. He’s a good man with good intentions. But what can he do when the people around him have bad intentions?” Bilawal asked.

In reference to remarks he made earlier this week, the party chief highlighted that the PPP did not start the “countdown” to the government’s collapse, but rather these elements within the ruling party.

“The PML-N’s fight is not with the PPP — it happens in elections, as it has before. The real fight is entirely different, because the PM, with his good intentions and actions, is undermined by a large part of the PML-N,” Bilawal alleged.

“A big part of the PML-N wants the PM to fight not only the opposition, but also his own allies.”

He then asked the audience: “Have there ever been elections held in six phases in Kashmir’s history? If Kashmir is one, then the election should have been held on a single day.”

Bilawal said the elections were being held in phases “so that there is calm and the elections are peaceful, free and fair”, before asking: “But in which phase were the elections free, fair or peaceful?”

“In truth, elections were carried out in phases so they could rig them. They knew that 10 seats were in their pocket from the start,” he alleged.

“With the 10 seats in their pocket, they robbed Mirpur, they robbed Muzaffarabad, and they’re looking at you, in Poonch. They are looking at Bagh. On August 10, they will find out that those in Poonch and Bagh hunt tigers.”

Elections are being held across AJK in three phases . Polls in Mirpur and Muzaffarabad divisions were held on July 27 and August 2, respectively.

The first phase of polling in Mirpur saw the PML-N secure nine of the 13 seats while the PPP won the remaining four.

In the second phase in Muzaffarabad, the PML-N bagged 15 more seats, while the PPP managed to add just six more to its tally.

The third phase in Poonch division was set for August 10. Poonch Division comprises 11 constituencies — three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch and two in Sudhnoti district.

However, earlier today, the AJK Election Commission revised the schedule for the third phase of elections in the region, saying polling would only be held in Poonch Division’s Bagh and Haveli districts on August 10 amid concerns over the law and order situation.

The electoral process in the constituencies of Poonch district and Sudhnoti’s Pallandri would not be held on August 10, the Election Commission said, adding that it reviewed the “current situation” regarding the scheduled elections in Poonch.

It noted that according to a report it received from the AJK home secretary, there were “concerns over the law and order situation in some areas of Poonch district and Pallandri district”.

The commission’s decision comes in the wake of clashes that took place between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Poonch district’s Rawalakot on July 27, which reportedly resulted in several casualties.

Rawalakot has been gripped by unrest since early June , with the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) staging sit-ins periodically.

The JAAC, which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now.

World.title: SCBA backs call for new provinces, calls it 'step forward' for better governance
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) — a premier lawyers’ body — on Friday voiced support for the controversial proposal recently put forward by Interior Minister Syed Mohsin Naqvi regarding the creation of new provinces in the country.

Recently, while addressing the Pakistan Economic Summit 2026, the interior minister had urged all political parties to resolve various national issues, including the question of creating new provinces. He termed this the only solution to improving the country’s overall condition, which he said had “collapsed”.

Speaking at the Full Court Reference held at the Supreme Court (SC) in honour of Justice Musarrat Hilali on the occasion of her laying down her judicial robes, SCBA President Haroonur Rashid said the association endorsed and supported the suggestion to create new provinces.

Headed by Chief Justice of Pakistan (CJP) Yahya Afridi, the reference was attended by SC judges both in person and via video link.

The reference was also attended by Additional Attorney General (AAG) Chaudhry Aamir Rehman, representatives of the SCBA and the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC), senior members of the legal fraternity, court officers, media representatives and others.

“The association believes that any constitutional measure for the creation of more provinces would be a step forward towards an enhanced governance system through devolved and equitable administration at the grassroots level, the creation of equal opportunities for parallel economic development, and stronger political stability in the country,” the SCBA president said.

He added that the creation of more provinces would also improve the standard of living by addressing the economic challenges faced by the people of the country.

Meanwhile, in its 250th meeting held in Islamabad on Friday, the PBC — the apex body of the legal fraternity — said it firmly believed that all constitutional matters must be addressed strictly within the framework of the Constitution.

The PBC deliberated upon the issue of the creation of new administrative units and provinces in the country. It reaffirmed through a resolution that the legal fraternity was committed to upholding the Constitution, and that members were of the unanimous view that the question of creating new provinces should be considered in accordance with the constitutional principles and procedures.

The resolution emphasised that all political parties, irrespective of their political differences, should act in the “larger national interest” and initiate a “comprehensive and meaningful dialogue” for the betterment of the country and its people.

The PBC resolved that, if the establishment of new provinces was deemed necessary, it must be carried out strictly in accordance with the Constitution through due parliamentary process and national consensus.

The PBC also authorised its Vice Chairman Pir Muhammad Masood Chishti and the chairman of its Executive Committee to organise a national seminar by inviting leaders of all political parties represented in Parliament, as well as representatives of provincial bar councils, for meaningful dialogue and to develop a broad-based national consensus. The seminar would aim to strengthen the federation, promote good governance, ensure equitable administrative and economic development, and improve the welfare of the common man.

On the other hand, the SCBA president said the association would continue supporting the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments.

He said the association believed that the amendments were an “important step towards ensuring parliamentary sovereignty, enhancing the separation of powers, and realising the concept that the judiciary should focus more on its fundamental constitutional responsibility of prompt dispensation of justice”.

He also requested President Asif Ali Zardari to immediately give his assent to the recent appointment and confirmation of the high court judges recommended by the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) during its meeting on July 20 and 21.

“SCBA believes that the appointment procedure adopted through the recent amendments were more balanced, comprehensive and transparent, since both the members of the judiciary and the Parliament were part of such a judicial process,” he said.

Rashid also expressed his trust and confidence in the performance of the JCP, saying that its recent decisions regarding the appointment of judges to the high courts were based on merit, as “competent individuals” had been recommended for the highest judicial offices.

Therefore, pendency in the grant of assent by the president may result in harming the Constitution as well as the interests of the country, he said.

During the reference, the AAG, SCBA president and PBC vice chairman paid rich tributes to Justice Hilali’s professional integrity, judicial acumen and unwavering commitment to the administration of justice. They acknowledged the respect and admiration she earned across the bench and the bar through her principled conduct, independence and distinguished service, and conveyed their heartfelt best wishes for the next chapter of her life.

In his address, CJP Afridi paid tribute to Justice Hilali, describing her judicial journey as one defined by “courage, perseverance and an unwavering commitment to justice”.

He observed that her career was remarkable not only for the high judicial offices she held, but also for the barriers she broke and the enduring example she set for generations of lawyers, particularly women aspiring to leadership roles within the legal profession.

“Justice Hilali’s career stands as a beacon of the growing participation and leadership of women in Pakistan’s justice sector,” Afridi said.

Her professional journey, he noted, demonstrated that integrity, dedication and professional excellence remained the “true hallmarks of judicial leadership” and could inspire future generations of women to pursue careers of distinction in law and justice.

The CJP also acknowledged Justice Hilali’s valuable contributions to strengthening the principles of judicial responsibility, institutional integrity, and public service throughout her tenure.

PBC condemns NCCIA’s detaining of Islamabad-based journalists

The PBC, in its Friday meeting, also strongly condemned the actions of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) in issuing notices to and detaining Islamabad-based journalists under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca).

The council demanded that the government should immediately withdraw all such illegal notices and refrain from any actions that undermine the constitutional guarantees of freedom of expression and freedom of the press.

“The legal fraternity has always stood in support of an independent and free media as a fundamental pillar of democracy and the rule of law, and will continue to oppose any attempt to intimidate, harass, or curtail the independence of the media,” it said.

World.title: Power consumers to pay 75 paisa per unit FCA in August bills
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) on Friday notified an additional burden of Rs9.8 billion on electricity consumers for the August billing period due to a fuel cost adjustment (FCA) of 75 paisa per unit.

The net average fuel cost in August would be around 41 paisa per unit higher than in July, when the FCA stood at Rs0.34 per unit.

In its notification, Nepra said it had decided that the positive FCA for June 2026, amounting to Rs0.7503 per kWh, would apply to all consumer categories that opted for prepaid tariffs, except lifeline consumers, electric vehicle charging stations and prepaid electricity consumers.

The adjustment applies to K-Electric (KE) as well as power distribution companies (Discos) that originated from Wapda.

The regulator said the adjustment would also apply to consumers under the incremental consumption package. Discos and KE are required to reflect the fuel charges adjustment for June 2026 in the billing month of August 2026.

The FCA is reviewed every month as per the tariff regime applicable across the country and is usually applicable to the consumer’s bills for one month only.

The Central Power Purchasing Agency (CPPA) had reported that the actual average fuel charges component for June 2026 was Rs8.9138/kWh, compared with the reference fuel charges component of Rs7.7138/kWh approved in the applicable notified consumer-end tariff.

Accordingly, it had demanded Rs1.20 per unit additional FCA for June 2026.

After certain adjustments, Nepra worked out the actual fuel component of the tariff at Rs8.4641, thereby allowing a lower FCA of Rs0.75 per unit in August instead of Rs1.20.

The power division and its entities had reported a 5.6 per cent decline in overall generation in June compared to the projected level.

Nepra expressed concern over partial loading charges amounting to Rs4.9 billion.

CPPA, however, argued that these charges were not due to operational inefficiencies but resulted from reduced daytime demand caused by rooftop solar generation.

Power plants were operated at partial load during solar hours and ramped up later to meet the evening increase in grid demand.

The power division warned that renewable power sources, such as wind and solar, may need to be curtailed in the future if daytime demand declines significantly in the coming years.

Under the tariff mechanism, changes in fuel cost are passed on to consumers only on a monthly basis through the automatic mechanism.

On the other hand, quarterly tariff adjustments — based on variation in power purchase price, capacity charges, variable operation and maintenance costs, use of system charges and impact of transmission and distribution losses — are built in the base tariff by the federal government.

Last week, the government indicated that it was working on another power tariff package as it sought about Rs1.20 per unit additional fuel cost from consumers to collect Rs15.7 billion in August for electricity consumed in June.

World.title: Italy defies Spanish demand to lift border curbs over Ceuta migrant crisis
World.content:
Spain threatened on Friday to impose restrictions on travellers from Italy unless Rome lifts by Sunday the border controls it introduced last week following a mass influx of migrants into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta.

Italy swiftly responded, saying it would not accept “ultimatums or impositions” from Madrid, adding that it would keep in place its suspension of Schengen rules for non-EU nationals arriving from Spain until at least August 15.
